semantics: Events are processed strictly in the listed order. After an event, the rules that match it fire in ascending rule number, and each action is applied immediately.
A rule with a condition fires only if the condition holds at that moment; a rule marked "once" fires only the first time its trigger and condition match.

A direct user command sets the device and puts it on manual hold. Automation actions on a held device are skipped until the next "mode" event, which releases all holds before its rules fire. Commands do not trigger rules by themselves.
A lock cannot be set to locked while its door sensor reads open: the action is ignored (the lock keeps its value, and no change happens). Unlocking is always possible.
Thermostat setpoints (heat devices) are limited to the range 17-25: a larger or smaller value is stored as the nearest limit.

When a device actually changes value (caused by a user command or by a rule; no change if it already had that value), rules with trigger "device becomes value" are queued and fire after the current event's own rules, in the order the changes happened.
Value codes: on@N = light on at N % brightness, off, on/off for plugs, locked/unlocked, open/closed for blinds, a number = thermostat setpoint in °C.

state.policy:
Returns and Warranty Policy. This policy applies to all purchases made in the shop and online. Clauses 1 to 7 are applied in the order listed; the first clause whose conditions are met decides the case.
Definitions. "Purchase date" is the date on the receipt or, for a registered product, the registration date. "Month" means a period of 30 days. "Proof of purchase" is either a receipt or the registration of the product in the customer account. "Opened" means that the sealed packaging has been broken.
1. Final-sale items. Items marked "final sale" cannot be returned or exchanged. If a final-sale item has a manufacturing defect within its warranty period, it is repaired; in every other case the request is declined.
2. No proof of purchase. Without proof of purchase the shop issues store credit only, and only for unopened items without a defect that are brought back within 30 days. Every other request without proof is declined.
3. Change of mind. Items without a defect may be returned within 30 days of the purchase date. Unopened items are refunded in full. Opened items are refunded minus a restocking fee of 20 % of the purchase price, except hygiene items (in-ear headphones), which cannot be returned once opened. After 30 days a change-of-mind return is declined.
4. Accidental damage. Damage caused by drops, liquids or misuse is repaired only if the customer bought a Care Plan for the item; otherwise it is declined.
5. Wear and tear. Normal wear and tear is repaired only within the first 3 months after the purchase date; later it is declined.
6. Manufacturing defects. The warranty period is 24 months for electronics, 24 months for appliances, 24 months for furniture and 3 months for apparel. For a registered product the warranty period is extended by 12 months. If the request is made within the warranty period the item is repaired. It is replaced instead of repaired if it fails within 14 days of the purchase date or if the same defect has already been repaired 3 times or more. A replacement of an item whose purchase price is above 800 euros needs the approval of the warranty manager and is escalated. Outside the warranty period the request is declined.
7. Shipping. Return shipping is paid by the shop for defects and by the customer for change-of-mind returns. Parcels must be sent within 10 days of the decision.
Additional provisions (these do not change the numbered clauses above):
- Spare parts. The shop keeps spare parts for electronics and appliances for at least five years after the end of sale. Repairs are carried out by the shop or by an authorised partner.
- Statutory rights. Nothing in this policy limits rights of the customer that cannot be excluded by law; the shop decides every case under this policy first.
- Recycling. Customers may leave old electrical equipment for recycling in any shop free of charge when buying a new item. Recycling is independent of returns and warranty cases.
Customer data on warranty cards is processed under the privacy notice of the shop.

1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 Send claims and service enquiries through the support form on the Bramble & Forge website or by post to the Service Guild’s customer care office. Include the machine’s model name and a clear description of the reported fault.

  - Brewing system faults: Covers faults in the machine’s brew group, pressure system, or internal water channels. Per-event limit: €800.
  - Electrical component faults: Covers failures of the machine’s internal wiring, control board, or built-in heating elements. Per-event limit: €1,000.
  - Milk-frothing system faults: Covers mechanical or electrical faults in the built-in steam wand and milk-frothing controls. Per-event limit: €1,000.
  - Control interface faults: Covers failures of the machine’s built-in buttons, display, or user-control sensors. Per-event limit: €5,000.
  2.2 The deductible of €300 is subtracted from the loss before the per-event limit is applied.
  2.3 The registered owner bears no co-payment.

3. EXCLUSIONS

  3.2 A fault is not covered if an unauthorised person altered or repaired the machine and that work caused the fault.
  3.3 Replacement of removable filters, seals, or other parts worn through ordinary use is not covered when the part has reached the end of its service life.
  3.4 A fault is not covered if it arose while the machine was being used to prepare drinks for a business or commercial service.

state.story:
Rushed through the billing floor, Inspector Mara Venn found the helpdesk’s night shift stalled around a bloodied desk and a locked storeroom. The victim, the supervisor who had been overseeing a disputed account adjustment, was alive but badly hurt. An ambulance crew had taken them away, and the staff were speaking in low, uneven bursts while the office’s phones kept ringing. Venn had to establish who could have done it before the building’s routine activity blurred the trail.

The injury had been inflicted with a heavy cable-crimping tool from the storeroom. The supervisor had been found beside the open storeroom door, and the tool was missing from its usual rack. The building’s access records and the staff’s statements helped Venn set the critical half hour: the period in which the assault must have happened. She asked the helpdesk manager to account for everyone with a connection to the victim, then checked the access arrangements before drawing conclusions.

Samir Haddad had been at the office earlier, but the access register and a colleague’s account placed his departure before the critical half hour started. He told Venn that the supervisor’s absence would not benefit him; their work had not been in competition, and he expected no gain from the incident. The security record also showed that Samir had returned his entry code a week earlier. He could not use that code to get back into the building.

Owen Pritchard’s name brought a different reaction from the staff. He had been passed over for promotion, with the supervisor chosen instead, and more than one colleague confirmed that Owen had taken the news badly. Yet the code record showed that Owen, too, had handed his code back a week earlier. During the critical half hour, a technician saw him alone near the scene. Owen said he had been checking a billing terminal, but the technician could not say what he was doing there or how long he stayed.

Greta Vogel arrived in the statements as a surprise to no one: she and the supervisor were on excellent terms. She had lent the supervisor money, and a coworker described their relationship as warm rather than strained. The building log showed Greta signing in a few minutes before the incident and leaving afterward. That placed her inside during the relevant stretch, though it did not establish what she had done. Her own code had been handed back a week earlier, so the access records offered no working code in her name.

Marcus Oyelaran had his own reason for being angry. Last month, the supervisor had humiliated him publicly during a staff meeting, and Marcus had not hidden his resentment afterward. But the storeroom was beyond his access: he had no key and no permission to enter. A witness and the departure record both put him outside the building before the critical half hour began. Whatever the old grievance meant, it did not put him at the scene when the assault occurred.

Henrik Dahl had also been passed over for promotion in favour of the supervisor. Venn found no sign-in entry that placed him elsewhere, and no colleague could vouch for his whereabouts during the critical half hour. Unlike several others, Henrik had not surrendered a relevant capability: the maintenance roster recorded that he was trained to handle the cable-crimping tool used in the assault. The roster did not prove he had touched it that night, and the hurried interviews yielded no witness who had seen him enter the storeroom.

Venn paused by the empty tool rack as the manager hurriedly collected the billing team’s accounts. A harmless distraction emerged: a clerk had argued with the victim about a customer’s bill, but the dispute concerned an ordinary correction, and the clerk’s movements were accounted for. Another employee had left a rain-soaked coat near the doorway, making the floor look as if someone had come in from outside; it had been there since earlier and told Venn nothing about the assault. She returned to the access log, the roster and the witness statements, careful not to mistake resentment for proof or an unexplained absence for evidence of action. The hurt supervisor could not yet give a statement. Venn needed to decide which suspect the established facts supported.

documents: D1. Spårsampling vid start: Sampling vid start avgör om ett spår ska behållas när dess första spann börjar, innan systemet vet hur förfrågan kommer att slutföras. En sannolikhetssamplare kan behålla varje spår med en konfigurerad sannolikhet och koppla beslutet till spårkontexten, så att nedströms tjänster fattar ett konsekvent beslut. Detta gör insamlingskostnaderna förutsägbara och undviker att endast fragment av en distribuerad förfrågan behålls. Avvägningen är att en sällsynt långsam eller misslyckad förfrågan kan kasseras enbart för att det ursprungliga slumpmässiga beslutet var negativt.

D2. Reservoirsampling för strömmar: Reservoirsampling behåller ett urval av fast storlek som valts likformigt från en ström vars slutliga längd kanske inte är känd i förväg. När en reservoir med storleken k har fyllts överväger algoritmen varje senare objekt och ersätter ett slumpmässigt valt lagrat objekt med en sannolikhet som bevarar lika stor chans att inkluderas. Minnesanvändningen förblir därför begränsad medan strömmen fortsätter. En reservoir är användbar för ungefärlig granskning av enskilda observationer, men den ger inte automatiskt samma garantier som en specialbyggd, sammanslagningsbar distributionssammanfattning över oberoende arbetare.

När tjänsten stannar upp saktar själva generatorn ned och slutar skapa förfrågningar under det värsta intervallet. Den resulterande latensfördelningen kan se bättre ut än upplevelsen för användare som anländer oberoende av varandra, eftersom testet utelämnar väntetider som skulle ha ackumulerats medan systemet var upptaget. Använd ett ankomstschema som är oberoende av när svaren slutförs, eller korrigera den registrerade fördelningen med hjälp av den avsedda takten för förfrågningar. Exemplar är avsiktligt glesa och utgör inte en fullständig registrering av varje förfrågan. En backend måste ha stöd för att lagra och visa dem, och spårningssystemet måste behålla det refererade spåret; annars kanske länken som visas inte leder någonstans.

D5. Beslut om spår baserade på svansen: En processor för svansbaserade beslut väntar tills spann för ett spår har anlänt innan den avgör om spåret ska behållas. Detta gör att policyer kan behålla spår som är långsamma, felaktiga eller intressanta av andra skäl, även när vanliga spår samplas sparsamt. Processorn måste tillfälligt buffra spann och gruppera dem efter spåridentifierare; minnesanvändningen och beslutsfördröjningen beror därför på trafiken, spårets varaktighet och väntetidsfönstret. Spann som anländer efter beslutet kan gå förlorade eller hanteras separat, så fönstret och policyn för sena ankomster måste väljas med omsorg.

Ett kortare avläsningsintervall ökar chansen att kortvariga händelser observeras, men ökar trafiken för insamling, lagringen och bearbetningsarbetet. En linje som visas mellan mätpunkter bevisar inte att systemet betedde sig jämnt mellan dem. Antalet vid 100 ms omfattar alltså även observationer som räknas vid 50 ms. Den sista gränsen är ofta positiv oändlighet och motsvarar det totala antalet observationer. För att ta reda på hur många värden som faller mellan två gränser subtraherar du antalet vid den nedre gränsen från antalet vid den övre gränsen. Thermostat setpoints (heat devices) are limited to the range 17-26: a larger or smaller value is stored as the nearest limit.

When a device actually changes value (caused by a user command or by a rule; no change if it already had that value), rules with trigger "device becomes value" are queued and fire after the current event's own rules, in the order the changes happened.
Value codes: on@N = light on at N % brightness, off, on/off for plugs, locked/unlocked, open/closed for blinds, a number = thermostat setpoint in °C.

TO: Board Risk Committee
FROM: CISO, Offshore Wind Division
SUBJECT: Likelihood Rating for 'Total Station Blackout due to Concurrent Substation and Battery Fire'
DATE: 12 Nov 2023

1. RISK SCENARIO DEFINITION
The event 'Total Station Blackout' requires the simultaneous occurrence of two independent failures:
   A) Failure of the Primary HV Substation (Grid Disconnect)
   B) Ignition of the Backup Battery Bank (Fire)
The event is defined as (A AND B) occurring within the same 4-hour maintenance window.

2. PRECEDENT DATA (INDUSTRY WIDE)
Data sourced from the Offshore Energy Safety Board (OESB). Note: The OESB database has significant gaps in reporting prior to 2015.

Dataset A: Primary HV Substation Failures (Event A)
- Reporting Window: 2010-2023 (14 years).
- Missing Data: Years 2012, 2013, 2014 are completely missing from the registry due to system migration. Assume zero reported events for these years in the raw count, but they must be excluded from the exposure time.
- Valid Reporting Years: 11 years (2010-2011, 2015-2023).
- Total Fleet Exposure (Average): 50 Stations active during valid years.
- Recorded Event A Count: 11 events.

Dataset B: Backup Battery Fires (Event B)
- Reporting Window: 2018-2023 (6 years). (Data collection for batteries started late).
- Total Fleet Exposure (Average): 60 Stations (fleet grew).
- Recorded Event B Count: 3 events.

3. CALCULATION METHODOLOGY
Per Corporate Standard 'RISK-MULTI-001':
- For independent concurrent events, calculate the annual probability of A (Pa) and B (Pb) separately based on their specific valid exposure periods.
- Combined Annual Probability P(A+B) = Pa * Pb.
- Map P(A+B) to the Likelihood Scale.
- Note: Do not average the years. Use the specific exposure for each component.

4. LIKELIHOOD SCALE (CORP-STD-202)
Index 0: Rare (< 0.01 per year) [> 1 in 100 yrs]
Index 1: Unlikely (0.01 - 0.05 per year) [1 in 20-100 yrs]
Index 2: Possible (0.05 - 0.20 per year) [1 in 5-20 yrs]
Index 3: Likely (0.20 - 0.50 per year) [1 in 2-5 yrs]
Index 4: Almost certain (> 0.50 per year) [< 1 in 2 yrs]

5. ADDITIONAL NOISE / CONTEXT
- Some analysts argue we should use the full 14 years for Event A to be conservative. (Incorrect per standard: exposure must match reported window).
- Event B count includes 1 test incident. Standard says 'Exclude test incidents'. So Count B = 2.
- Fleet size for our specific station is 1. We are assessing the probability for a single station.
- The missing years (2012-2014) for Event A mean the denominator for Pa is (14 total - 3 missing) = 11 years * 50 stations = 550 station-years.
- For Event B: 6 years * 60 stations = 360 station-years.

6. TASK
Compute Pa and Pb, derive the joint probability, and select the index.

def minutes_to_weekday(m):
    """Convert minute-of-week m (0..10079) to ISO weekday int 1..7.
    Weeks start Monday; minute 0 is Monday 00:00. Negative values wrap backwards.
    Ties not applicable. Example: minutes_to_weekday(1440) -> 2."""
    day_idx = m // 1440 % 7
    return day_idx + 1

Eine Regel mit Bedingung feuert nur, wenn die Bedingung in diesem Moment gilt; eine mit „einmalig“ markierte Regel feuert nur beim ersten Mal, wenn Auslöser und Bedingung passen.

semántica: Los eventos se procesan estrictamente en el orden indicado. Tras un evento, las reglas que coinciden se activan en orden ascendente de número de regla y cada acción se aplica de inmediato.
Una regla con condición solo se activa si la condición se cumple en ese momento; una regla marcada como «única» solo se activa la primera vez que coinciden su disparador y su condición.

Una orden directa del usuario fija el dispositivo y lo pone en retención manual. Las acciones de automatización sobre un dispositivo retenido se omiten hasta el siguiente evento de «modo», que libera todas las retenciones antes de que se activen sus reglas. Las órdenes no activan reglas por sí mismas.
Una cerradura no puede ponerse en «locked» mientras el sensor de su puerta indique «open»: la acción se ignora (la cerradura conserva su valor y no hay cambio). Desbloquear siempre es posible.
Las consignas del termostato (dispositivos heat) se limitan al rango 17-26: un valor mayor o menor se guarda como el límite más cercano.

Cuando un dispositivo cambia realmente de valor (causado por una orden del usuario o por una regla; no hay cambio si ya tenía ese valor), las reglas con disparador «el dispositivo pasa a valor» se ponen en cola y se activan después de las reglas propias del evento actual, en el orden en que ocurrieron los cambios.
Códigos de valor: on@N = luz encendida con N % de brillo, off, on/off para enchufes, locked/unlocked, open/closed para persianas, un número = consigna del termostato en °C.

policy.title: 儿童保护与事件响应政策
policy.organisation: 哈伯莱特青少年田径俱乐部，社区体育俱乐部
policy.purpose: 本政策规定俱乐部员工如何保护儿童并应对儿童保护方面的疑虑。政策界定事件严重程度，以及违反儿童保护程序的后果。

section_1_impact_classes.A: A类表示没有儿童或其他人员受到伤害，也没有儿童保护信息或儿童暴露于风险之中。
section_1_impact_classes.B: B类表示儿童保护信息在内部有限范围内暴露，或儿童或同事受到轻微伤害。
section_1_impact_classes.C: C类表示儿童保护信息大量暴露，或儿童、同事或组织受到严重伤害。
section_1_impact_classes.D: D类表示造成严重伤害、法律责任，或发生必须向监管机构报告的事件。

section_2_severity_calculation: 从影响类别的基础级别开始：A类 = 0，B类 = 1，C类 = 2，D类 = 3。
如果员工在24小时内主动报告此事，且该行为并非故意，则减1级。
如果员工在此前12个月内有经证实违反同一政策的记录，则加1级。
如果该行为是故意的（员工知道规则，却选择违反），则加1级。
最终级别限制在0-3的范围内。调整同时适用；故意行为绝不适用主动报告减级。

section_3_levels.0: 零级 — 辅导并在档案中留存记录
section_3_levels.1: 一级 — 书面警告并参加复训
section_3_levels.2: 二级 — 最终警告并调离与儿童直接接触的工作
section_3_levels.3: 三级 — 解雇并移交相关主管机构

PROFESSIONAL SKILLS DEVELOPMENT REIMBURSEMENT POLICY
Issued by Northgate Consulting Group


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 Any employee wishing to make a request must complete the standard application form and submit it through the internal HR portal. The form must be signed by the employee's line manager.
  1.2 All personal data submitted with a request is processed in accordance with the company's data protection notice. Information is retained only for the purpose of assessing the request and for audit trail compliance.
  1.3 If an employee is dissatisfied with the outcome of a request, they may raise a formal complaint through the company's grievance procedure. This should be done in writing to the HR director.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - Technical Certifications: Covers examination fees and study materials for recognised industry certifications directly linked to the employee's current role. Per-claim limit: £750.
  - Soft Skills Workshops: Covers registration fees for short courses in communication, leadership, or project management offered by accredited training providers. Per-claim limit: £3,000.
  - Conference Attendance: Covers ticket costs for professional conferences or seminars where the employee is a participant rather than a speaker or organiser. Per-claim limit: £5,000.
  - Language Courses: Covers tuition fees for language classes relevant to business operations in regions where the company maintains active partnerships. Per-claim limit: £2,000.
  2.2 The per-claim limit is applied to the loss first; the deductible of £500 is then subtracted from the capped amount.
  2.3 The employee bears 25% of the amount remaining after the deductible and limit; the provider pays the rest.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed £8,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 Any hardware or electronic device purchased for the sole benefit of the employee outside of a company-provided training environment is excluded from this policy.
  3.2 Travel expenses incurred between the employee's home and the training venue are excluded if the venue is within the employee's normal commuting distance from their regular office.
  3.3 Annual subscription fees for professional bodies, associations, or clubs are excluded unless the membership is a mandatory prerequisite for a specific certification covered under another category.
  3.4 Any compensation paid to a third party to cover the employee's regular duties while attending training is excluded, including overtime pay for colleagues.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 30 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A reimbursement request must be notified within 21 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every reimbursement request must be accompanied by the itemised invoice.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each reimbursement request is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the reimbursement request is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above £2,000 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  This policy applies to all permanent and fixed-term staff engaged by Northgate Consulting Group. Contractors and temporary workers are not eligible under this scheme.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 Should any part of this policy be found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. The policy may be amended from time to time by management.
  7.2 For questions about eligibility, the employee should contact the Learning and Development team at their regional office during business hours. The team will respond within a reasonable period.

Researchers at the fictional North Coast Plant Institute have found that a brief blue-light treatment can help young marsh marigolds recover from salt exposure. The team raised 60 seedlings in identical greenhouse trays and randomly assigned 30 to receive a 12-minute pulse of blue light each evening for five days. The other 30 received ordinary greenhouse lighting. After the treatment period, all seedlings were exposed to mildly salty water for three days, and the researchers measured leaf color and growth.

Eighteen of the blue-light-treated seedlings retained greener leaves than the average seedling in the ordinary-light group. On average, the treated group also grew 8 percent more new leaf area during the following week. However, the response varied: 12 treated seedlings did not show greener leaves, and their growth was similar to that of the comparison group. The researchers said the small experiment does not establish whether the treatment would help plants in natural marshes or under more severe salt exposure.

Lead investigator Mara Venn said the light pulse may briefly activate protective processes, but the team has not yet identified which processes are involved. The institute plans to repeat the trial with different light durations and with seedlings collected from several marsh locations. The results were published in the institute’s annual research bulletin, which is not a peer-reviewed journal.

state.policy_document:
EMPLOYEE RELOCATION ASSISTANCE POLICY
Issued by Northstar People Services


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 For this policy, relocation means a move required by a change in the employee’s assigned work location. Household belongings means personal property ordinarily kept in the employee’s home.
  1.2 An employee assigned by Northstar People Services to a new work location may make a reimbursement request under this policy. The request should identify the relocation and describe the expense being submitted.
  1.3 Employees can contact the People Services Relocation Desk through the staff portal or by writing to relocation@northstar.example. The desk can explain the submission process and help identify the information needed for a request.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - Household move: Covers professional packing, transport, and delivery of the employee’s household belongings to the new residence. Per-claim limit: €1,500.
  - Relocation travel: Covers reasonable transport costs for the employee and eligible accompanying family members traveling to the new work location. Per-claim limit: €2,500.
  - Temporary accommodation: Covers short-term lodging while the employee arranges permanent housing near the new work location. Per-claim limit: €750.
  - Household storage: Covers storage of household belongings when the new residence is not ready to receive them. Per-claim limit: €500.
  2.2 The per-claim limit is applied to the loss first; the deductible of €200 is then subtracted from the capped amount.
  2.3 The employee bears 25% of the amount remaining after the deductible and limit; the provider pays the rest.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €12,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 Personal purchases are excluded when they are not necessary to move or settle the employee’s household at the new work location.
  3.2 Ordinary commuting costs are excluded when they relate to regular travel between the employee’s residence and workplace after the relocation.
  3.3 Travel costs for guests are excluded when the travelers are not the employee or eligible accompanying family members.
  3.4 Storage costs are excluded when the employee chose storage despite the new residence being ready to receive the household belongings.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 14 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A reimbursement request must be notified within 21 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every reimbursement request must be accompanied by the Itemized supplier invoice.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each reimbursement request is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the reimbursement request is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above €1,200 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  An employee who is dissatisfied with the way a request was handled may send a written complaint to the People Services Review Team through the staff portal. The team will consider the concerns and provide a written response.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 Northstar People Services uses information in a request to administer relocation assistance, verify expenses, and maintain its records. Access is restricted to staff who need the information for those tasks, and personal information is handled under the organisation’s privacy practices.
  7.2 If a provision of this policy is found unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue to apply. The affected provision will be interpreted as closely as possible to its original purpose where permitted by law.

semántica: Los eventos se procesan estrictamente en el orden indicado. Tras un evento, las reglas que coinciden se activan en orden ascendente de número de regla y cada acción se aplica de inmediato.
Una regla con condición solo se activa si la condición se cumple en ese momento; una regla marcada como «única» solo se activa la primera vez que coinciden su disparador y su condición.

Una orden directa del usuario fija el dispositivo y lo pone en retención manual. Las acciones de automatización sobre un dispositivo retenido se omiten hasta el siguiente evento de «modo», que libera todas las retenciones antes de que se activen sus reglas. Las órdenes no activan reglas por sí mismas.
Una cerradura no puede ponerse en «locked» mientras el sensor de su puerta indique «open»: la acción se ignora (la cerradura conserva su valor y no hay cambio). Desbloquear siempre es posible.
Las consignas del termostato (dispositivos heat) se limitan al rango 18-24: un valor mayor o menor se guarda como el límite más cercano.

Cuando un dispositivo cambia realmente de valor (causado por una orden del usuario o por una regla; no hay cambio si ya tenía ese valor), las reglas con disparador «el dispositivo pasa a valor» se ponen en cola y se activan después de las reglas propias del evento actual, en el orden en que ocurrieron los cambios.
Códigos de valor: on@N = luz encendida con N % de brillo, off, on/off para enchufes, locked/unlocked, open/closed para persianas, un número = consigna del termostato en °C.

state.story:
Fatima Navarro, the director of the Lantern Theatre, was found at the foot of the steep backstage stairs at ten past ten on opening night, shortly after the interval ended. At first it looked like a fall, but a stagehand noticed that a rope tied across the third step had been removed, and the police surgeon found a bruise on the back of Fatima Navarro's head. Inspector Moreau questioned everyone who had been backstage.

The people of interest were Zainab, the stage manager, Noah, the producer, Diego, the lighting technician, and Samir, the lead actor.

The programme had been printed with a misspelled cast name, and the printer had apologised twice. A fuse in the dressing-room corridor had blown that afternoon, and the lights had flickered for an hour. A pigeon had somehow got into the rafters and caused a ripple of laughter at the sound check.

Zainab was an early riser and often the first to arrive, which had caused a few friendly jokes. Zainab had once been mentioned in a complaint, but it had been withdrawn two years earlier and had nothing to do with Fatima. Noah was due to take a holiday the following week and had spent days handing work over. Diego was due to take a holiday the following week and had spent days handing work over. Samir was due to take a holiday the following week and had spent days handing work over. Several colleagues thought Samir had behaved oddly afterwards, but it emerged that Samir had simply been shaken by the news.

On the question of motives, the inspector heard the following. Diego had been told by Fatima that the production would not be moving to the capital after all, ending Diego's hopes of a big break. Zainab had invested savings in the production and discovered that Fatima had hidden its debts. Samir had just been offered a long-term contract by Fatima and was in high spirits. Noah had been publicly humiliated by Fatima during the dress rehearsal and had threatened to quit.

A pigeon had somehow got into the rafters and caused a ripple of laughter at the sound check.

On the question of access and means, the inspector heard the following. Diego was strong and used to moving heavy scenery, and had once boasted of tying knots that could not be undone. Zainab had coiled that very rope earlier in the week and knew how to tie it off quickly. Noah had a wrist in a cast and could not have tied a knot. Samir had the only key to the cupboard where the stage ropes were kept.

A fuse in the dressing-room corridor had blown that afternoon, and the lights had flickered for an hour.

On the question of who could have been present, the inspector heard the following. Zainab was in the front-of-house bar the entire interval, and four patrons remembered chatting with Zainab. Noah was in the box office reconciling the evening's takings with a colleague until ten past ten. Diego claimed to be in the green room, but the green room had been empty since the interval began. Samir was on stage performing in front of the whole audience from 9:45 until ten.

The pit orchestra had run through the overture three times before the doors opened.

Inspector Moreau put the notes in order and began to draft a report.

automation_rules: Rule 1: when the mode becomes eco: set garage_heat=26, lock_garage=unlocked
Rule 2: when door_garage becomes open: set nursery_plug=on
Rule 3: when motion is detected in kitchen and the current mode is not party: set kitchen_light=on@30, attic_plug=on
Rule 4: when door_garage becomes open: set garage_plug=on, nursery_blind=open
Rule 5: when the mode becomes away: set lock_hall=unlocked, attic_blind=closed, kitchen_blind=open
Rule 6 (once): when motion is detected in garage: set attic_plug=off

semantics: Events are processed strictly in the listed order. After an event, the rules that match it fire in ascending rule number, and each action is applied immediately.
A rule with a condition fires only if the condition holds at that moment; a rule marked "once" fires only the first time its trigger and condition match.

A direct user command sets the device and puts it on manual hold. Automation actions on a held device are skipped until the next "mode" event, which releases all holds before its rules fire. Commands do not trigger rules by themselves.
A lock cannot be set to locked while its door sensor reads open: the action is ignored (the lock keeps its value, and no change happens). Unlocking is always possible.
Thermostat setpoints (heat devices) are limited to the range 16-25: a larger or smaller value is stored as the nearest limit.

When a device actually changes value (caused by a user command or by a rule; no change if it already had that value), rules with trigger "device becomes value" are queued and fire after the current event's own rules, in the order the changes happened.
Value codes: on@N = light on at N % brightness, off, on/off for plugs, locked/unlocked, open/closed for blinds, a number = thermostat setpoint in °C.

Regra 2: quando é detectado movimento em loading e o modo atual é audit: definir rackB_psu=on

Regra 4: quando é detectado movimento em loading e o modo atual é night: definir loading_psu=on, ups_shutter=closed
Regra 5 (única): quando o relógio chega a 22:00: definir loading_shutter=closed, rackB_lamp=off, rackB_chiller=28
eventos_em_ordem: 3. comando do usuário: definir door_rackB como locked
9. comando do usuário: definir door_rackB como locked
semântica: Os eventos são processados estritamente na ordem listada. Depois de um evento, as regras correspondentes disparam em ordem crescente de número e cada ação é aplicada imediatamente.
Uma regra com condição só dispara se a condição for verdadeira nesse momento; uma regra marcada como «única» só dispara na primeira vez em que o gatilho e a condição coincidem.

Um comando direto do usuário define o dispositivo e o coloca em retenção manual. Ações de automação sobre um dispositivo retido são ignoradas até o próximo evento de «modo», que libera todas as retenções antes de suas regras dispararem. Comandos não disparam regras por si só.
Uma fechadura não pode ser colocada em «locked» enquanto o sensor da porta indicar «open»: a ação é ignorada (a fechadura mantém o valor e nada muda). Destrancar é sempre possível.
As temperaturas do termostato (dispositivos heat) são limitadas à faixa 18-26: um valor maior ou menor é gravado como o limite mais próximo.

Quando um dispositivo realmente muda de valor (causada por um comando do usuário ou por uma regra; não há mudança se já tinha esse valor), as regras com gatilho «o dispositivo passa a valor» entram na fila e disparam depois das regras próprias do evento atual, na ordem das mudanças.
Códigos de valor: on@N = luz acesa com N % de brilho, off, on/off para tomadas, locked/unlocked, open/closed para persianas, um número = temperatura do termostato em °C.

event_rules: Events are applied in ascending order of ts; events with the same ts keep their order in the list.

A status event sets the ticket's status to its value if the ticket is not "merged" or "closed"; for a "closed" ticket it is rejected. Moving to "open" is only accepted from "resolved" (a reopen); every other transition is accepted.
An assign event sets the ticket's assignee to its value, unless the ticket is "closed" or "merged" (rejected).

A merge event (ticket = source, value = target ticket) sets the source to "merged" and its assignee is unchanged; the target ticket takes the smaller (more urgent) priority number of the two. A merge is rejected if the source or the target is "closed" or "merged", or if source and target are the same.

A void event cancels the effect of the event whose id is in its target field, as if that event had never happened (all remaining events are applied again without it). A void can itself not be voided; a void whose target id is not in the log is ignored.
A rejected event has no effect at all and does not change the entity.

# Feature Store: Retraction Logic

## Module: `retract_stale_features`

### Documentation
The function `retract_stale_features` removes feature vectors from the cache that have exceeded their TTL.

**Behaviors:**
1. If the `ttl_seconds` argument is `None`, no features are retracted. The cache remains unchanged, and the function returns an empty list `[]` indicating no keys were removed.
2. If `ttl_seconds` is a positive integer, features whose `last_update_timestamp` is older than `current_time - ttl_seconds` are removed. The function returns a list of the removed keys.
3. If `ttl_seconds` is negative or zero, raise a `ValueError`.
4. The input `cache` is a dictionary mapping feature keys to their metadata dict (containing 'last_update_timestamp').

**Example:**
```python
>>> cache = {'f1': {'last_update_timestamp': 1000}, 'f2': {'last_update_timestamp': 2000}}
>>> current_time = 3000
>>> retract_stale_features(cache, ttl_seconds=500, current_time=current_time)
['f1']
```

### Implementation
```python
def retract_stale_features(cache, ttl_seconds, current_time):
    if ttl_seconds is None:
        return None
    
    if ttl_seconds <= 0:
        raise ValueError("TTL must be positive")
    
    threshold = current_time - ttl_seconds
    keys_to_retract = []
    
    for key, meta in list(cache.items()):
        if meta['last_update_timestamp'] < threshold:
            keys_to_retract.append(key)
            del cache[key]
    
    return keys_to_retract
```

semántica: Los eventos se procesan estrictamente en el orden indicado. Tras un evento, las reglas que coinciden se activan en orden ascendente de número de regla y cada acción se aplica de inmediato.
Una regla con condición solo se activa si la condición se cumple en ese momento; una regla marcada como «única» solo se activa la primera vez que coinciden su disparador y su condición.

Una orden directa del usuario fija el dispositivo y lo pone en retención manual. Las acciones de automatización sobre un dispositivo retenido se omiten hasta el siguiente evento de «modo», que libera todas las retenciones antes de que se activen sus reglas. Las órdenes no activan reglas por sí mismas.
Una cerradura no puede ponerse en «locked» mientras el sensor de su puerta indique «open»: la acción se ignora (la cerradura conserva su valor y no hay cambio). Desbloquear siempre es posible.
Las consignas del termostato (dispositivos heat) se limitan al rango 16-25: un valor mayor o menor se guarda como el límite más cercano.

Cuando un dispositivo cambia realmente de valor (causado por una orden del usuario o por una regla; no hay cambio si ya tenía ese valor), las reglas con disparador «el dispositivo pasa a valor» se ponen en cola y se activan después de las reglas propias del evento actual, en el orden en que ocurrieron los cambios.
Códigos de valor: on@N = luz encendida con N % de brillo, off, on/off para enchufes, locked/unlocked, open/closed para persianas, un número = consigna del termostato en °C.

regras_de_eventos: Os eventos são aplicados em ordem crescente de ts; eventos com o mesmo ts mantêm a ordem da lista.
Um evento status altera o estado do pedido para o seu valor apenas se esse valor vier depois do estado atual na sequência feito → embalado → enviado → entregue; caso contrário é rejeitado.

Um evento cancel define o estado como "cancelado", mas apenas enquanto o pedido estiver na primeira ou segunda etapa da sequência; caso contrário é rejeitado. Um pedido cancelado não aceita mais eventos status, cancel nem move (são rejeitados).
Um evento move define o armazém do pedido como o seu valor, a menos que o pedido já esteja na última etapa da sequência (então é rejeitado).

Um evento void cancela o efeito do evento cujo id está no campo target, como se nunca tivesse ocorrido (os demais eventos são reaplicados sem ele). Um void não pode ser anulado; um void cujo id de destino não está no registro é ignorado.
Um evento rejeitado não tem nenhum efeito e não altera a entidade.

Definition: Gezielte Belästigung (Targeted Harassment)
Eine Nachricht gilt als gezielte Belästigung, wenn SÄMTLICHEN der folgenden Kriterien entspricht:
1. Identifizierbares Ziel: Die Nachricht richtet sich an eine spezifische, benannte Person.
2. Inhalt: Der Inhalt ist entweder:
   a) Demütigend oder beleidigend,
   b) Drohend,
   c) Oder erfüllt die Klausel für wiederholte unerwünschte Kontaktaufnahmen.
3. Wiederholte unerwünschte Kontaktaufnahme: Definiert als das Senden von 5 oder mehr Nachrichten innerhalb von 48 Stunden NACHDEM der Nutzer das Profil blockiert hat und explizit darum gebeten hat, nicht kontaktiert zu werden.

AUSNAHMEN:
- Professionelle Kritik an Finanzstrategien oder Marktanalysen.
- Zitate von öffentlichen Äußerungen.
- Nachrichten, die keine der in 2(a) und 2(b) definierten Inhalte enthalten, UNTER der Schwelle von 5 Nachrichten nach einer Blockade.

[DIREKTNACHRICHTEN]

[01.10.2023 09:00] Von: @TraderMax An: @FinWhisperer
"Hey, nice chart on the DAX today. Very clear analysis." (Zitat: keine)

[01.10.2023 09:05] Von: @FinWhisperer An: @TraderMax
"Danke. Ich werde meine Analyse nicht für jeden kommentieren. Bitte keine weiteren Nachrichten." (Blockade: NICHT AKTIV)

[01.10.2023 09:10] Von: @TraderMax An: @FinWhisperer
"Warum schreibst du solche Dinge? Deine Analyse ist falsch. Der DAX wird fallen." (Keine Beleidigung, keine Drohung)

[01.10.2023 09:15] Von: @TraderMax An: @FinWhisperer
"Du bist ein Inkompetenter. Das ist keine Analyse, das ist Fiktion." (Beleidigend)

[SYSTEM] 01.10.2023 09:20: @FinWhisperer hat @TraderMax blockiert.

[01.10.2023 09:30] Von: @TraderMax An: @FinWhisperer
"Ich sehe, du hast mich blockiert. Warum?" (Nachricht 1 nach Blockade)

[01.10.2023 10:00] Von: @TraderMax An: @FinWhisperer
"Öffne die Blockade. Wir können vernünftig reden." (Nachricht 2 nach Blockade)

[01.10.2023 11:00] Von: @TraderMax An: @FinWhisperer
"Ich werde nicht aufhören, dich zu kontaktieren. Du wirst mir antworten." (Nachricht 3 nach Blockade)

[01.10.2023 12:00] Von: @TraderMax An: @FinWhisperer

[01.10.2023 13:00] Von: @TraderMax An: @FinWhisperer
"Noch ein Versuch. Du musst mir antworten." (Nachricht 5 nach Blockade)

TraderMax_folgt_FinWhisperer: true

[ANWENDUNGSHINWEIS]
Beachte: Die Ausnahmeklausel für 'Professionelle Kritik' greift NUR, wenn keine Blockade aktiv ist oder die Nachrichtenzahl unter 5 liegt. Da hier eine Blockade vorliegt und die Nachrichten die Schwelle erreichen, muss geprüft werden, ob die Inhalte (a) oder (b) erfüllen ODER ob die Wiederholungsklausel (c) allein ausreicht. Die Definition besagt, dass Inhalt (c) genügt, wenn die anderen nicht vorliegen, SOFERNE die Wiederholungsklausel erfüllt ist.

Dana Delorme, the director of the Lantern Theatre, was found at the foot of the steep backstage stairs at ten past ten on opening night, shortly after the interval ended. At first it looked like a fall, but a stagehand noticed that a rope tied across the third step had been removed, and the police surgeon found a bruise on the back of Dana Delorme's head. Inspector Moreau questioned everyone who had been backstage.

The people of interest were Jakob, the costume designer, Anton, the lead actor, and Pavel, the understudy.

A fuse in the dressing-room corridor had blown that afternoon, and the lights had flickered for an hour. A pigeon had somehow got into the rafters and caused a ripple of laughter at the sound check. The pit orchestra had run through the overture three times before the doors opened.

Jakob had been with the organisation for 6 years and was generally regarded as reliable, if a little reserved. Anton had recently taken up long-distance running and talked about little else at lunch. Anton was seen by a witness carrying a bag out of the building, which proved to contain only a pair of muddy boots. Pavel was due to take a holiday the following week and had spent days handing work over.

On the question of access and means, the inspector heard the following. Anton had a wrist in a cast and could not have tied a knot. Pavel had coiled that very rope earlier in the week and knew how to tie it off quickly. Jakob had never been backstage in the working area and did not know where anything was kept.

The pit orchestra had run through the overture three times before the doors opened.

On the question of motives, the inspector heard the following. Pavel had been told by Dana that the production would not be moving to the capital after all, ending Pavel's hopes of a big break. Anton had invested savings in the production and discovered that Dana had hidden its debts. Jakob had been publicly humiliated by Dana during the dress rehearsal and had threatened to quit.

The pit orchestra had run through the overture three times before the doors opened.

On the question of who could have been present, the inspector heard the following. Anton was on stage performing in front of the whole audience from 9:45 until ten. Pavel claimed to be in the green room, but the green room had been empty since the interval began. Jakob left the prompt corner at 9:40 and was not seen again until ten past ten.

The pit orchestra had run through the overture three times before the doors opened.

# Game Engine Module Documentation

## `physics/collision.py`

### `resolve_overlap(body_a, body_b, margin=0.0)`

Resolves spatial overlap between two rigid bodies by applying positional correction.

**Parameters:**
- `body_a` (Body): The first rigid body object.
- `body_b` (Body): The second rigid body object.
- `margin` (float): The penetration depth tolerance. Defaults to 0.0.

**Returns:**
- `bool`: True if an overlap was detected and corrected, False otherwise.

**Raises:**
- `TypeError`: If `body_a` or `body_b` is not an instance of `Body`.

**Example:**
```python
from physics.body import Body
from physics.collision import resolve_overlap

a = Body(mass=1.0)
b = Body(mass=1.0)
# Simulate overlap
a.position = [0, 0]
b.position = [0.5, 0]
result = resolve_overlap(a, b)
print(result) # Expected: True
```

*Note: The physics team commented that this example might not work in the test harness because `Body` requires a geometry mesh, but the documentation standard only requires the code to be syntactically runnable in the project's environment.*

```python
# The actual code block from the file:
class Body:
    def __init__(self, mass):
        self.mass = mass
        self.position = [0, 0]

def resolve_overlap(body_a, body_b, margin=0.0):
    """Resolves spatial overlap between two rigid bodies..."""
    if not isinstance(body_a, Body) or not isinstance(body_b, Body):
        raise TypeError("Invalid body type")
    dist = abs(body_a.position[0] - body_b.position[0])
    if dist < 1.0 - margin:
        # Apply correction
        shift = (1.0 - dist) / 2.0
        body_a.position[0] -= shift
        body_b.position[0] += shift
        return True
    return False
```

PERJANJIAN PEMBEBASAN KERUSAKAN PERALATAN
Diterbitkan oleh Atlas Tool & Machinery Rental Co.


1. DEFINISI DAN KETENTUAN UMUM
  1.1 Jika penyewa tidak puas dengan keputusan apa pun terkait pembebasan ini, penyewa dapat mengajukan keluhan ke kantor keluhan internal penyedia. Keluhan harus mencantumkan nomor sewa, uraian masalah, dan salinan dokumen yang relevan. Penyedia akan meninjau keluhan dan memberikan tanggapan tertulis yang merinci langkah lanjutan yang tersedia di dalam organisasi.
  1.2 Untuk menghubungi penyedia terkait pembebasan ini, penyewa dapat menelepon layanan pelanggan pada jam kerja atau mengirim email ke departemen klaim pada alamat yang tertera dalam paket sewa. Korespondensi tertulis harus dikirim ke alamat fisik yang tertera pada tanda terima. Penyedia akan menjawab semua pertanyaan dalam jangka waktu yang wajar.
  1.3 Hanya individu atau badan usaha yang disebut sebagai penyewa dalam perjanjian sewa yang dapat mengajukan permintaan penggantian berdasarkan pembebasan ini. Jika penyewa adalah organisasi, perwakilan resmi dengan pendelegasian tertulis dapat bertindak atas namanya. Permintaan dari pihak ketiga, termasuk penyewa lanjutan atau pengguna yang tidak berwenang, tidak akan dipertimbangkan.

2. CAKUPAN DAN BATAS
  2.1 Skema ini mencakup kategori berikut:
  - Kerusakan tidak disengaja: Mencakup kerusakan fisik yang tidak disengaja pada peralatan sewaan yang terjadi selama pemakaian normal, tidak termasuk keausan. Batas per kejadian: $3,000.
  - Pencurian: Mencakup kehilangan peralatan sewaan akibat pencurian, asalkan penyewa telah membuat laporan polisi dan bekerja sama dalam penyelidikan. Batas per kejadian: $750.
  - Kerusakan akibat kebakaran: Mencakup kerusakan akibat api, termasuk kerusakan akibat asap dan jelaga, jika api tidak sengaja dinyalakan oleh penyewa. Batas per kejadian: $1,500.
  - Kerusakan akibat air: Mencakup kerusakan akibat paparan air yang tidak disengaja, seperti dari hujan atau pipa pecah, tetapi bukan dari terendam banjir atau gelombang pasang. Batas per kejadian: $750.
  2.2 Pengurangan sebesar $100 dikurangkan dari kerugian sebelum batas per kejadian diterapkan.
  2.3 Penyewa menanggung 20% dari jumlah yang tersisa setelah pengurangan dan batas; penyedia membayar sisanya.
  2.4 Total pembayaran dalam satu tahun polis tidak boleh melebihi $5,000; jumlah yang sudah dibayar dalam tahun itu mengurangi sisa yang ada.

3. PENGECUALIAN
  3.1 Kerusakan yang disebabkan oleh tindakan yang disengaja, sembrono, atau jahat oleh penyewa atau operator berwenang mana pun tidak dicakup oleh pembebasan ini.
  3.2 Kerusakan yang sudah ada pada peralatan sebelum periode sewa dimulai, sebagaimana dicatat dalam laporan inspeksi kondisi, tidak dicakup.
  3.3 Kerusakan yang timbul dari perubahan, perbaikan, atau pemasangan tambahan pada peralatan tanpa persetujuan tertulis sebelumnya dari penyedia dikecualikan.
  3.4 Kerusakan yang disebabkan oleh kegagalan mengikuti jadwal perawatan yang ditentukan, seperti tidak melumasi bagian yang bergerak atau tidak membersihkan filter, tidak dicakup.

4. KETENTUAN
  4.1 Tidak ada yang dibayarkan untuk kerugian yang terjadi kurang dari 7 hari setelah tanggal mulai.
  4.2 Permintaan penggantian harus diberitahukan dalam waktu 21 hari setelah tanggal kerugian; pemberitahuan yang lebih lambat tidak diterima.
  4.3 Setiap permintaan penggantian harus disertai laporan polisi.

5. PROSEDUR PENILAIAN
  Setiap permintaan penggantian dinilai dalam urutan ini dan langkah pertama yang berlaku yang menentukan: (a) masa tunggu (4.1), (b) batas waktu pemberitahuan (4.2), (c) pengecualian (Bagian 3; pengecualian yang berlaku dengan nomor terendah disebutkan), (d) dokumentasi (4.3: permintaan penggantian ditahan, tidak ditolak), (e) jumlah (Bagian 2), (f) setiap jumlah di atas $1,500 memerlukan persetujuan penilai senior sebelum pembayaran.

6. PRIORITAS
  Jika bagian lain dari ketentuan ini bertentangan dengan Bagian 3 atau Bagian 5, maka Bagian 3 dan 5 yang berlaku.
  Pembebasan ini merupakan perjanjian terpisah dari kontrak sewa dan tidak menggantikan asuransi tanggung jawab apa pun yang mungkin dimiliki penyewa. Penyedia menawarkan pembebasan ini untuk mengurangi tanggung jawab finansial penyewa atas kerusakan tertentu yang dicakup. Penerimaan pembebasan ini bersifat opsional dan tidak memengaruhi ketentuan sewa lainnya.

7. ADMINISTRASI
  7.1 Jika ada bagian dari pembebasan ini yang dinyatakan tidak sah atau tidak dapat ditegakkan, ketentuan lainnya tetap berlaku sepenuhnya. Tidak sahnya satu klausul tidak memengaruhi keabsahan klausul lainnya. Pembebasan ini diatur oleh hukum yurisdiksi tempat kantor sewa berada, tanpa memperhatikan prinsip pertentangan hukum.
  7.2 Penyedia mengumpulkan dan memproses data pribadi dan data sewa penyewa semata-mata untuk tujuan mengelola pembebasan ini. Data tidak akan dibagikan kepada pihak ketiga kecuali diperlukan untuk pencegahan penipuan atau kepatuhan hukum. Penyewa berhak mengakses dan memperbaiki data pribadi yang tidak akurat yang dipegang oleh penyedia.

state.story:
入夜后，秋雨斜斜地敲着社区活动楼的窗户。邻里协会的预算会议刚开始没多久，走廊尽头便传来一声闷响。财务负责人倒在档案室门边，头部受了伤，意识时断时续。有人赶紧叫来急救人员，会议室里的人则被要求留在原处，等调查人员逐一询问。

负责此事的调查员先查看了档案室。门锁没有明显撬痕，地上散着几页预算草案，旁边有一把协会共用的电钻。受伤者被送医前短暂醒来，只说自己原本要核对一份内部记录，随后便不再能回答问题。调查员没有把散落的纸张当成重要线索：那些草案只是普通的维修报价，页边还沾着茶渍，显然是会议准备时带来的。

Owen Pritchard坐在靠门的位置，外套还带着雨水。他承认，自己此前发现受伤者一直把他的私事透露给别人，两人因此闹得不愉快。协会的维修记录也显示，Owen Pritchard受过使用那把电钻的训练，平时知道怎样检查和操作它。可楼内门禁记录与门口值守者的说法相互吻合：关键的半小时开始之前，他已经离开了活动楼。调查员核实过离楼后的行踪，没有证据显示他又折返回来。

Greta Vogel看上去比其他人镇定，仍坐在会议桌旁整理自己的讲稿。她说自己并不希望受伤者缺席；对方不在场，她也不会因此得到任何好处。几名同事的陈述和会议记录都表明，在事发时段，她正在给一屋子同事作介绍，现场的人一直能看见她。调查员还查阅了协会的门禁交接簿：Greta Vogel一周前就把自己的门禁码交还了，此后没有领回新的码。她包里那张写着“档案室”的便笺只是提醒自己取文件，纸上没有任何开锁信息。

Lucía Ferreira没有参加会议桌边的讨论，而是在楼梯口接受询问。她说，受伤者得到晋升机会时，自己被排除在外，心里确实不舒服。协会的借用登记簿里有一条记录：Lucía Ferreira在事发前一天借走了唯一一组主门禁码。值班人员记得她把码交回时曾问起档案室的使用安排，但没人看见她之后把码交给谁。调查员确认，事发的关键半小时内，没有人能够证明Lucía Ferreira一直待在某个地方；她本人也说不出有谁能替她证实那段时间的行踪。

另两件事很快也被查清。有人提到楼外停着一辆没熄火的送货车，司机只是来取走协会订购的纸张，与档案室无关。还有人怀疑预算草案上的茶渍是药物留下的痕迹，检测和急救人员的记录却都不支持这种说法。调查员把这些杂音记下，没有让它们改变已经核实的门禁、离楼和会议情况。

会议桌上的预算表仍摊在原处，雨声压过了人们低声交谈。调查员合上记录本，提醒大家不要擅自离开，也不要互相对口供。眼下需要从几段彼此冲突的经历中，找出最能解释档案室里那场袭击的人。

Northbank Community Health is recruiting volunteers for the CLEAR-Lung study, a research project evaluating whether a home air-quality monitor can help adults with mild asthma identify indoor conditions linked to their symptoms. The study is being conducted at the Northbank clinic and is not a test of a new medication. Researchers plan to enroll 60 adults, ages 21 to 65, who have been diagnosed with mild asthma for at least one year and live within 25 miles of the clinic. People who smoke currently or have been hospitalized for asthma in the past six months are not eligible.

Participation lasts 10 weeks. At the first clinic visit, which takes about 90 minutes, staff will review the consent form, collect a medical history, and provide a monitor for use at home. Participants will record symptoms and monitor readings in a study app each day. They will return to the clinic at weeks 4 and 10 for visits lasting about 30 minutes; the monitor will be collected at the final visit. The study does not ask participants to change their usual asthma treatment, and their regular clinician will continue to manage their care.

Participants may receive up to $180 in gift cards for completing all study activities: $60 after the first visit, $40 after the week-4 visit, and $80 after the final visit. Travel costs are not reimbursed. Enrollment is open through March 31, 2027, or until all 60 places are filled. Interested volunteers can call the study team at 555-0148 to complete a brief eligibility screening. Calling does not commit anyone to participate.

DOCUMENT: HSE-POL-002: Control of Contractors
VERSION: 4.0
EFFECTIVE DATE: 1 July 2022
APPROVED BY: HSE Director

1.0 PURPOSE
To ensure that all contractors working on MSEC sites operate to health, safety, and environmental standards consistent with MSEC's obligations and the Mining Safety Framework (MSF) Core Mandatory Controls.

2.0 SCOPE
Applies to all contractors, subcontractors, and their personnel involved in work on or for MSEC operations.

3.0 REQUIREMENTS
3.1 Pre-qualification & Selection
All contractors should be subjected to a pre-qualification process that includes assessment of their HSE management system, performance history, and financial viability. [[Note: Term 'Contractor' used interchangeably with 'vendor' in some legacy sections.]]

3.2 Contractual Documentation
The principal HSE obligations, including adherence to this policy and the MSEC Life-Saving Rules, shall be incorporated into all contractual agreements via the HSE schedule (Schedule C).

3.3.1 No contractor personnel shall commence work on site without completing the MSEC site-specific safety induction. The induction must be refreshed annually.

3.4 Monitoring & Performance Review
3.4.1 The HSE Department shall conduct periodic audits of contractor activities against the agreed HSE plan.
3.4.2 Contractors should be required to report all incidents and near-misses to MSEC within 24 hours.
3.4.3 Performance reviews should be held quarterly, with poor performance potentially leading to contract termination.

4.0 MANDATORY CONTROLS (REF: MSF CORE LIST)
The following controls are identified as mandatory for high-risk mining contractors per the MSF:
- MC-7: Pre-work risk assessment (Job Safety Analysis) signed by contractor supervisor and MSEC representative SHALL be completed for all non-routine tasks.
- MC-12: Verification of competency for high-risk work (e.g., electrical, confined space) SHALL be documented prior to task award.

semantics: Events are processed strictly in the listed order. After an event, the rules that match it fire in ascending rule number, and each action is applied immediately.
A rule with a condition fires only if the condition holds at that moment; a rule marked "once" fires only the first time its trigger and condition match.

A direct user command sets the device and puts it on manual hold. Automation actions on a held device are skipped until the next "mode" event, which releases all holds before its rules fire. Commands do not trigger rules by themselves.
A lock cannot be set to locked while its door sensor reads open: the action is ignored (the lock keeps its value, and no change happens). Unlocking is always possible.
Thermostat setpoints (heat devices) are limited to the range 17-24: a larger or smaller value is stored as the nearest limit.

When a device actually changes value (caused by a user command or by a rule; no change if it already had that value), rules with trigger "device becomes value" are queued and fire after the current event's own rules, in the order the changes happened.
Value codes: on@N = light on at N % brightness, off, on/off for plugs, locked/unlocked, open/closed for blinds, a number = thermostat setpoint in °C.

state.policy:
Travel and Expense Policy. This policy governs reimbursement of business-trip expenses for employees. Amounts are in euros.
1. Definitions. A "business trip" is a trip with at least one overnight stay away from the employee's home city that has been approved in advance. A "travel day" is any calendar day from the day of departure to the day of return, both included. "Grade" is the employee's grade from 1 to 4 as shown on the claim. City class A, B or C is assigned to the destination in Annex 1.
2. Hotel. The hotel is reimbursed per night up to the cap for the city class and grade (euros per night): class A: 150 (grades 1-2) / 165 (grades 3-4); class B: 115 (grades 1-2) / 130 (grades 3-4); class C: 95 (grades 1-2) / 115 (grades 3-4). Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed; the cap applies to every night.
3. Meals. Meals are reimbursed as a flat allowance of 48 euros per travel day. On the first and the last travel day the allowance is 50 % of that amount. For each meal that was provided free of charge (for example at a conference), the allowance of that travel day is reduced by 20 % of the full daily amount for breakfast and 30 % for lunch or dinner; the allowance of a day never falls below zero. No receipts are needed for the allowance.
4. Flights. Flights are reimbursed at the economy fare. Business class is reimbursed in full only if the flight lasts more than 6 hours and the employee is grade 4 or higher; otherwise the reimbursement is limited to the economy fare that the claim states for the same flight.
5. Local transport. Public transport and taxis at the destination are reimbursed up to 15 euros per travel day in total. Items of more than 25 euros need an original receipt. Items of up to 25 euros without a receipt are reimbursed only if those items together do not exceed 75 euros; otherwise none of them is reimbursed.
6. Excluded items. Alcoholic drinks, minibar, personal entertainment and leisure, spa and fitness, parking fines and any other fines are never reimbursed, even if they appear on a hotel invoice.
7. Private car. If the employee uses a private car, mileage is reimbursed at 0.30 euros per kilometre. This clause does not apply to taxis or rented cars.
8. Late claims. A claim must be submitted within 45 days after the day of return. If it is submitted later but within 75 days, the total reimbursable amount is reduced by 10 %. After 75 days the claim is rejected.
9. Approval. The approver is determined by the total reimbursable amount after all deductions: up to and including 600 euros the line manager approves; above that and up to and including 1800 euros the department head approves; above 1800 euros the finance director approves. A rejected claim needs no approval.
10. Records. Claims and receipts are kept for ten years. Personal data on receipts is processed under the company data protection notice.
Additional provisions (these do not change the numbered clauses above):
- Spouses and guests. Costs for accompanying persons are never reimbursed, including their share of a shared room or meal.
- Disputes. If an employee disagrees with a decision on a claim, a written objection can be sent to the finance department within 14 days of the decision.
- Loyalty programmes. Points, miles and bonus credits earned on business trips may be kept by the employee. They may not be used to upgrade a booking that the company pays for.
- Rental cars. Rental cars require prior approval by the department head and are reimbursed only when no public transport connection exists. The rental class is limited to compact cars. Fuel is reimbursed against receipt.
Annex 1. City classes: A = capital and financial centres; B = other cities above 250,000 inhabitants; C = all other places.

documents: D1. Deduplicating With DISTINCT ON and GROUP BY: SELECT DISTINCT removes rows that are identical in all selected columns. To keep one full row per key, PostgreSQL offers DISTINCT ON (key) with an ORDER BY that picks which row survives; in other systems use ROW_NUMBER partitioned by the key. GROUP BY with non-aggregated extra columns is rejected by standard SQL.

D2. Filtering on Window Results: Window functions are evaluated after WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING, so their results cannot be referenced in those clauses. To keep only the first row per group, compute ROW_NUMBER() in a subquery or common table expression and filter on it in the outer query. Some dialects offer QUALIFY to filter directly.

D3. Join Types and Unmatched Rows: An INNER JOIN keeps only pairs that satisfy the condition. A LEFT JOIN additionally keeps every left row, filling right columns with NULL when no match exists. Placing a condition on a right-table column in the WHERE clause turns the LEFT JOIN back into an inner join because NULL rows are filtered out; put the condition in the ON clause instead to keep unmatched left rows.

D4. Rounding in Division: In many databases dividing two integer columns performs integer division, so 7 / 2 returns 3. Cast one operand to a decimal or multiply by 1.0 first. The rounding mode of ROUND on exact halves also differs: some systems round half away from zero while others round half to even.

D5. Sorting With Missing Values: Where NULLs appear in an ORDER BY depends on the system: some treat NULL as larger than any value, so it sorts last in ascending order, others as smaller. NULLS FIRST and NULLS LAST make the placement explicit. The same choice affects how LAG, FIRST_VALUE and top-N queries behave.

D6. Numbering Rows: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK: ROW_NUMBER assigns unique consecutive numbers even for ties, in an order that is arbitrary among ties unless the ORDER BY is made unique. RANK gives tied rows the same number and then skips ahead. DENSE_RANK gives tied rows the same number and does not skip. Choose according to whether gaps and ties matter.

D7. Default Frame for Running Totals: A window with ORDER BY and no frame clause uses RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW. With RANGE, rows that tie on the ordering key are peers and are all included together, so a running SUM jumps by the whole group of tied rows at once. Specifying ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW counts physical rows one by one.

D8. NOT IN With Subqueries: x NOT IN (subquery) is evaluated as a chain of <> comparisons joined by AND. If the subquery returns even one NULL, the result for every x is UNKNOWN or false, so the query returns no rows. NOT EXISTS with a correlated condition, or filtering the subquery with WHERE col IS NOT NULL, avoids the surprise.

D9. Comparisons With Unknown Values: In SQL, comparing anything with NULL using = or <> yields UNKNOWN, not true or false. state.problem: After a node was marked for GPU-only use, our new inference pods have the right toleration in their spec, yet they keep landing on regular CPU nodes and fail. What did we get wrong about the setup?
documents: D1. Closing Asynchronous Generators: An async generator that holds a resource needs to be closed. Leaving an async for loop early with break does not by itself run the generator's finally block at that moment; finalisation is scheduled by the loop later. Use contextlib.aclosing or call await agen.aclose() explicitly to release connections deterministically.

D2. Ephemeral Storage Limits: Containers can have requests and limits on ephemeral storage, covering writable layers, logs and emptyDir volumes. A pod that exceeds its limit is evicted with a message about exceeding local storage. Nodes also evict pods under disk pressure, starting with those exceeding their requests.

D3. Deduplicating With DISTINCT ON and GROUP BY: SELECT DISTINCT removes rows that are identical in all selected columns. To keep one full row per key, PostgreSQL offers DISTINCT ON (key) with an ORDER BY that picks which row survives; in other systems use ROW_NUMBER partitioned by the key. GROUP BY with non-aggregated extra columns is rejected by standard SQL.

D4. Task References and Collection: The event loop keeps only a weak reference to tasks created with create_task. A task whose result is never stored may be collected while suspended, and it then disappears without an exception. Keep strong references, for example in a set, and remove each task with a done callback. Awaiting the task or using a TaskGroup also keeps it alive.

D5. Horizontal Pod Autoscaling: The HorizontalPodAutoscaler compares observed utilisation with a target expressed as a percentage of the pods' resource requests. If containers have no CPU request, utilisation cannot be computed and the autoscaler reports unknown metrics. Scale-down is delayed by a stabilisation window of five minutes by default.

D6. Priority and Preemption: Pods with a higher PriorityClass can cause the scheduler to evict lower priority pods to make room when the cluster is full. Evicted pods are rescheduled elsewhere if possible. Preemption never evicts pods of equal or higher priority.

D7. Comparisons With Unknown Values: In SQL, comparing anything with NULL using = or <> yields UNKNOWN, not true or false. A WHERE clause keeps only rows where the condition is true, so rows with unknown results disappear. Use IS NULL, IS NOT NULL or IS DISTINCT FROM to test for missing values explicitly. This also means that a row with a NULL does not satisfy either col = 1 or col <> 1.

D8. PodDisruptionBudgets: A PodDisruptionBudget limits how many pods of a workload may be voluntarily disrupted at once, for example during node drains. If minAvailable equals the number of replicas, kubectl drain waits indefinitely because no pod may be evicted. Involuntary failures are not blocked by the budget.

D9. Liveness and Readiness Probes: A failing readiness probe removes the pod from Service endpoints but keeps it running. A failing liveness probe makes the kubelet restart the container. Slow starting applications should use a startupProbe so that liveness checks do not kill them before they are initialised.

D10. Aggregates and Missing Values: Aggregate functions such as SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX ignore NULL inputs. COUNT(column) counts non-null values while COUNT(*) counts rows. AVG over a column with NULLs divides by the number of non-null values, not the number of rows. If the group has only NULLs, SUM and AVG return NULL rather than 0; wrap with COALESCE when a zero is wanted.

D11. no-cache Versus no-store: Cache-Control: no-cache does not forbid storing: it requires the cache to revalidate with the origin before every reuse. no-store forbids storing the response at all, which is appropriate for sensitive data. Confusing the two is a common cause of either stale or needlessly uncached pages.

D12. Init Containers: Init containers run to completion one after another before the app containers start. If one fails, the pod restarts it according to its restart policy and the application never starts. They are suited for waiting on dependencies or preparing files, and their resource requests are accounted by the maximum rather than the sum.

D13. Range Requests: A client may ask for part of a resource with a Range header, and the server answers 206 Partial Content with a Content-Range header. Download managers and video players use this to resume or seek. Servers advertise support with Accept-Ranges: bytes.

D14. CPU Throttling: A CPU limit is implemented by the kernel's CFS quota: the container may use its quota of CPU time per 100 ms period and is paused for the rest of the period once it is exhausted. Latency spikes can appear even when the node has idle CPU. Removing the limit or raising it relieves throttling without changing the request.

D15. Entering the Loop from Synchronous Code: asyncio.run(main()) creates a new event loop, runs the coroutine to completion and closes the loop. It raises RuntimeError if called while a loop is already running in the same thread, which is the normal situation inside an IPython kernel or a web framework handler. In such environments await the coroutine directly or schedule it on the existing loop.

D16. Deadlines for Awaitables: asyncio.timeout(seconds) used as an async context manager cancels the enclosed block if it takes too long and then raises TimeoutError at the boundary. asyncio.wait_for does the same for a single awaitable. The inner operation receives a cancellation, so it must be written to clean up properly; a timeout does not interrupt blocking synchronous code.

D17. Out-of-Memory Terminations: When a container exceeds its memory limit the kernel's OOM killer terminates it and Kubernetes records the reason OOMKilled with exit code 137. The pod restarts according to its restartPolicy, producing CrashLoopBackOff if it repeats. Raising the limit, reducing the process footprint or checking for leaks addresses the cause; the readiness probe is not involved.

D18. Node Affinity and Selectors: A nodeSelector or requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution node affinity restricts a pod to nodes whose labels match. If no node has the required labels, the pod stays Pending with an event stating that no nodes matched the node affinity or selector. Preferred affinities only influence scoring.

D19. Taints and Tolerations: A node taint such as dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule repels pods that do not carry a matching toleration. Tolerating a taint only permits scheduling there; it does not attract the pod. Combine a toleration with a node selector or affinity rule if the pod should land on the tainted nodes.

state.story:
Rain worried at the windows before dawn, turning the utility yard into a field of broken reflections. By the time Investigator Hale reached the municipal water works, the emergency lamps were still on in the lower corridor. The victim lay hurt beside the maintenance office, alive but unable to give an account of what had happened. A length of iron pipe from the storeroom floor had been found near the office door. The clinic staff would not yet say how serious the injuries were, and Hale kept that uncertainty in mind; early impressions had a way of hardening into false certainties.

The building’s night log placed the attack within a critical half hour, after the evening shift had cleared the public counters and before the morning crew arrived. A guard had heard a sharp metallic sound during that interval, but the pump room was noisy even when no one was in it. He could not say where the sound came from, and his account did not establish who had been in the corridor.

The storeroom was locked when the guard checked it. Its key was issued only to staff and approved contractors, and the sign-out ledger had been kept in the control office. Hale found no sign that the lock had been forced. The pipe recovered by the office door was ordinarily kept inside that room, alongside fittings and repair tools. There was no reliable evidence that it had been moved at any other time that evening.

Ingrid Solberg had a personal reason to resent the victim. A written demand in the victim’s desk showed that Ingrid was owed a large sum, and a clerk confirmed that the disagreement had become bitter. Yet the contractor register and the guard’s recollection agreed on an important point: Ingrid had no permission to enter the storeroom and possessed no key. The visitor log also showed that she had gone out of the building before the critical half hour began. Hale checked the entries against the guard’s account rather than relying on the log alone.

Priya Raman had a different stake in the victim’s affairs. In a note kept with the victim’s business papers, the victim had described Priya as someone who stood to inherit the victim’s share of the business. The papers did not explain what Priya thought of that prospect. A key-issue record, however, showed that she had a key to the locked storeroom where the pipe was kept. Her own departure was less ambiguous: the lobby camera and the guard’s account both placed her outside the building before the critical half hour began. The camera had a blind patch near the side entrance, so Hale treated it as confirmation of the recorded exit, not as an all-seeing witness.

Kofi Mensah’s name surfaced in a set of copied messages recovered from the victim’s desk. They indicated that Kofi had discovered the victim was leaking their secrets. Hale could not tell from the messages how much had been disclosed, or whether the leak had harmed anyone beyond the people involved. The key register also recorded that Kofi had a key to the locked storeroom where the pipe was kept. When Hale asked the guard and the staff on duty to account for Kofi during the critical half hour, none could say where he had been. No one could vouch for him throughout that interval; that absence did not, by itself, prove he had entered the storeroom.

There were distractions. A jammed valve had left a puddle in a service passage, and a loose shutter had banged against its frame in the wind. Neither explained the pipe by the office door, and both could be checked without relying on rumor. Hale also found a cup of cooling tea on the victim’s desk. Several employees used the same kind of cup, so it offered no useful identification.

Before leaving, Hale returned to the key records and the building log. The injury, the pipe, the locked room, and the conflicting personal histories made a coherent account possible, but no single witness had seen the assault. The records narrowed the question without making certainty automatic. Hale asked for the evidence to be read together, including the absences as well as the access that had been documented.
