state.problem: Ons DevOps-team gebruikt een gedeelde crontab op een server met veel taken. We hebben zojuist een taak toegevoegd die wordt uitgevoerd op 0 0 * * 1, wat middernacht op maandag betekent. Maar de taak werd ook uitgevoerd op de 1e van de maand, en dat was geen maandag. Dat veroorzaakte een conflict met een andere taak. We verwachtten dat de taak alleen op maandagen zou worden uitgevoerd. Hoe behandelt standaard-cron de velden voor dag van de maand en dag van de week samen? We moeten ons schema aanpassen om deze dubbele uitvoering te voorkomen.
documents: D1. Anacron voor systemen die niet 24/7 draaien: Anacron is een aanvullend hulpmiddel naast cron voor machines die niet altijd aan staan, zoals laptops of desktops. Het houdt per taak bij wanneer deze voor het laatst is uitgevoerd en voert gemiste taken na het opstarten uit, met een vertraging. Het gebruikt een spoolmap om tijdstempels op te slaan. In tegenstelling tot cron plant het geen taken op een specifiek tijdstip, maar zorgt het ervoor dat taken minstens één keer per vastgestelde periode worden uitgevoerd (bijv. dagelijks, wekelijks). De configuratie staat in /etc/anacrontab met de velden: periode in dagen, vertraging in minuten, taak-id, opdracht. Het voert taken achtereenvolgens uit en activeert bij het opstarten alle taken waarvan de uitvoeringstijd is aangebroken. Voor servers die altijd aan staan, heeft cron de voorkeur vanwege de nauwkeurigheid. Gebruik anacron voor onderhoudstaken zoals het roteren van logbestanden.

D2. Deterministische volgorde van meerdere taken: Cron garandeert geen uitvoeringsvolgorde tussen taken die voor hetzelfde tijdstip zijn gepland. De daemon kan ze in willekeurige volgorde starten, mogelijk gelijktijdig. Gebruik voor taken met onderlinge afhankelijkheden één wrapper-script dat ze achtereenvolgens uitvoert, of gebruik een afhankelijkheidsbeheerder. Een back-up gevolgd door een synchronisatie moet bijvoorbeeld in één cron-vermelding staan. Een andere mogelijkheid is dat de tweede taak controleert of er een voltooiingsmarkering aanwezig is. Ga niet uit van een alfabetische volgorde of de volgorde van bestanden. Op sommige systemen is de volgorde van crontab-regels van belang, maar POSIX garandeert dit niet. Gebruik voor betrouwbare pipelines een workflowtool zoals Airflow of Make.

D3. Exitcodes en e-mailmeldingen: Cron stuurt standaard een e-mail met de uitvoer van een taak als deze stdout of stderr produceert, ongeacht de exitcode. Sommige systemen sturen alleen een e-mail bij een niet-nul-exitcode als u een mailwrapper gebruikt. U kunt uitvoer omleiden naar /dev/null of een logbestand om spam te voorkomen. Als u expliciet een melding wilt ontvangen bij een fout, kunt u een opdracht gebruiken zoals 'job; echo $?' of een monitoringtool gebruiken. Cron gebruikt de exitcode zelf niet om iets te beslissen; het geeft deze alleen door aan het mailsysteem. Sommige cron-implementaties hebben echter een variabele MAILTO om de ontvanger in te stellen. Als een taak stilzwijgend mislukt, merkt u dat mogelijk niet tenzij u de logboeken controleert. Overweeg een sentinelbestand te gebruiken.

D4. Volgorde van velden in een cron-expressie: Een cron-schema is een tekenreeks met vijf of zes door witruimte gescheiden velden. De standaardvolgorde is minuut, uur, dag van de maand, maand, dag van de week en optioneel jaar. Elk veld accepteert getallen, bereiken, lijsten en stapwaarden. In Vixie cron worden de velden voor dag van de maand en dag van de week gecombineerd met OF; een taak wordt dus uitgevoerd als aan een van beide voorwaarden is voldaan. Dit is een veelvoorkomende bron van verwarring, omdat sommige systemen EN-semantiek gebruiken. Test altijd met een dry-runtool voordat u iets implementeert. '0 0 1 * 1' wordt bijvoorbeeld uitgevoerd op de eerste dag van de maand en ook elke maandag, niet alleen wanneer de eerste dag een maandag is. Begrijp de prioriteitsregels van uw cron-implementatie om onverwachte activeringen te voorkomen.

D5. Cron-taken willekeurig spreiden om een piekbelasting te voorkomen: Wanneer veel taken voor dezelfde minuut zijn gepland, starten ze allemaal tegelijk, waardoor de CPU- en I/O-belasting piekt. Een gebruikelijke techniek is om in het taakscript een willekeurige vertraging toe te voegen, zoals sleep $((RANDOM % 60)). Zo wordt de belasting gespreid. Wees echter voorzichtig: als de vertraging langer duurt dan het volgende interval, kan er overlap ontstaan. Een andere methode is een cron-vermelding te gebruiken met een willekeurige minuut die tijdens de installatie wordt gegenereerd. Bijvoorbeeld: '15 * * * *' versus '45 * * * *'. Dit is geen fail-safe voor globale synchronisatie; u moet de coördinatie tussen servers regelen. Gebruik een taakplanner zoals Jenkins als u gedistribueerde taakverdeling nodig hebt.

D6. Gemiste uitvoeringen overslaan na uitval: Wanneer een cron-daemon niet actief is op een gepland tijdstip, zet deze de gemiste aanroep niet in de wachtrij. Na het opnieuw starten voert deze alleen toekomstige schema's uit. Dit gedrag voorkomt een achterstand van verouderde taken. Sommige systemen bieden echter een inhaaloptie (zoals -catchup in Airflow of anacron voor dagelijkse taken). Als uw taak kritiek is en ook na uitval precies één keer moet worden uitgevoerd, gebruik dan een aparte planner of een statusbestand. Vertrouw er niet op dat cron gemiste uitvoeringen aanvult. Als een taak bijvoorbeeld om 2:00 AM was gepland en de server tot 3:00 AM uitgeschakeld was, wordt de taak niet om 3:00 AM uitgevoerd. U moet de taak handmatig starten of een tool gebruiken die gemiste tijdstippen registreert.

D7. Langlopende taken en de volgende cron-uitvoering: Als een cron-taak langer duurt dan het interval tussen geplande uitvoeringen, start de volgende activering standaard gelijktijdig een tweede instantie. Dit kan leiden tot concurrentie om bronnen of beschadiging van gegevens. Sommige cron-implementaties hebben een instelling voor het maximumaantal instanties (bijv. cronie's MAX_INSTANCES), of u kunt de opdracht omwikkelen met een vergrendeling. Standaard-Vixie cron heeft geen ingebouwde optie 'overslaan als actief'. U moet dit zelf implementeren. Houd er ook rekening mee dat de overlappende instantie mogelijk een inconsistente status leest. Een robuust ontwerp is het gebruik van één langlopende daemon die werk ophaalt, of het instellen van een vlag 'running' die de volgende aanroep controleert en waarna deze stilzwijgend wordt beëindigd. Meet de taakduur en stel de intervallen daarop af.

D8. Een eenmalig gemiste taak oplossen met @reboot: De macro @reboot in crontab voert een taak één keer uit wanneer de cron-daemon start, meestal bij het opstarten van het systeem. Dit is handig voor het initialiseren van services of het opruimen van tijdelijke bestanden. De taak wordt echter niet uitgevoerd als de daemon opnieuw wordt gestart zonder dat het systeem opnieuw wordt opgestart (bijv. service cron restart). U kunt ook een periodieke terugvaloptie toevoegen om dit op te vangen. De taak @reboot wordt uitgevoerd met dezelfde omgeving als andere cron-taken. Als u na een specifieke uitval een eenmalige taak nodig hebt, kunt u die niet via cron plannen, omdat cron geen optie heeft om 'eenmalig bij de volgende start' uit te voeren naast @reboot. Gebruik voor een echte eenmalige taak de opdracht 'at'.

state.source:
Northstar Ledger 4.8 is available as of October 6. This release adds a saved-view feature to the activity dashboard: users can name a set of filters and reopen it from a new menu labeled “Saved views.” Each workspace can store up to 12 saved views, and existing dashboard filters are not changed by the update.

The release also introduces CSV export for the audit log. Exports include event time, actor, action, and object ID; they do not include free-text notes. The export control appears only to users with the Audit Manager role. Administrators can grant that role through Settings > Access, as before.

For organizations using the Northstar Sync agent, version 2.6 or later is required to use the new audit-log export. The web dashboard and saved views do not require an agent update. Teams on older agent versions can continue using the existing audit-log screen while they plan an upgrade; the release does not set a shutdown date for that screen.

To move to 4.8, administrators should first check the Sync agent version if they intend to use CSV export. The web update is applied automatically, so no client download is needed. Northstar recommends trying the export with a small date range before scheduling a recurring internal report. The release notes do not report performance benchmarks or changes to dashboard loading times.

state.story:
La pioggia di fine autunno rigava le finestre della falegnameria quando l’ispettore Riva arrivò nel laboratorio. Il proprietario, Elias Varga, era stato trovato ferito accanto al banco di montaggio, dietro una porta che dava sul reparto di finitura. Era cosciente, ma non riusciva a spiegare che cosa fosse accaduto. Sul pavimento c’erano una sedia rovesciata e alcuni trucioli; non risultavano segni di effrazione. L’arnese usato per colpirlo era uno degli utensili pesanti del laboratorio, rimesso al suo posto dopo l’aggressione.

La responsabile del turno raccontò che Varga era stato trovato durante il giro di controllo, quando il reparto era ormai quasi vuoto. L’ispettore fece delimitare l’area e chiese i registri delle presenze, le annotazioni sui codici d’accesso e le dichiarazioni di chi aveva lavorato con la vittima. Il momento dell’aggressione fu circoscritto a una mezz’ora precisa: per valutare gli spostamenti di ciascuno, disse, non bastava sapere chi avesse avuto un dissapore con Varga o chi conoscesse gli strumenti.

Tomás Navarro era già uscito dall’edificio prima che cominciasse quella mezz’ora. Nel suo colloquio non emerse alcuna lite con Varga; anzi, il proprietario lo aveva elogiato di recente per la qualità delle sue finiture. Il registro dei codici confermava inoltre che Tomás aveva restituito il proprio codice una settimana prima. Un collega ricordò che, dopo quell’elogio, Tomás aveva parlato con evidente soddisfazione del lavoro svolto e non aveva mostrato risentimento verso il titolare.

Anche Kofi Mensah aveva lasciato la falegnameria prima dell’intervallo in cui si era verificato il fatto. La sua posizione nei confronti di Varga, tuttavia, era diversa. Il mese scorso, durante una riunione aperta ai dipendenti, Varga lo aveva umiliato davanti agli altri, rimproverandolo con durezza per un errore di lavorazione. Più di un collega ricordava l’imbarazzo di Kofi e il silenzio con cui aveva incassato quelle parole. Il registro delle consegne indicava che, il giorno prima dell’aggressione, Kofi aveva preso in prestito l’unico codice principale, quello che consentiva l’accesso ai locali. La restituzione risultava annotata più tardi, sempre tra i movimenti di quel giorno.

Ingrid Solberg non si era allontanata dal proprio posto di lavoro per raggiungere il reparto di finitura. Nel momento dell’aggressione stava tenendo una presentazione in una sala con i colleghi; i presenti confermarono di averla vista parlare davanti al gruppo. La promozione che lei sperava di ottenere era stata assegnata a Varga, una decisione che aveva lasciato in lei un’amarezza difficile da nascondere. Eppure, il registro riportava che Ingrid aveva riconsegnato il suo codice una settimana prima. Durante la presentazione, secondo chi vi aveva partecipato, non aveva interrotto l’esposizione né lasciato la sala.

La posizione di Samir Haddad richiese più verifiche. Aveva scoperto che Varga stava rivelando ad altri i suoi segreti, circostanza che aveva incrinato il rapporto fra i due. Samir sapeva anche usare con competenza l’utensile coinvolto nell’aggressione: la scheda di formazione attestava che era stato istruito nella sua manipolazione. Il registro degli ingressi lo collocava nell’edificio pochi minuti prima dell’inizio dell’incidente, mentre quello delle uscite mostrava che se n’era andato soltanto dopo. Nessuno dei colleghi sentiti seppe precisare che cosa avesse fatto nel reparto durante quel periodo.

Owen Pritchard, infine, non aveva un vantaggio evidente dalla scomparsa di Varga. Le persone interrogate non seppero indicare alcun beneficio che avrebbe potuto ricavare dall’assenza del proprietario. Come Kofi, Owen risultava aver preso in prestito l’unico codice principale il giorno prima; la registrazione del passaggio e quella della restituzione erano entrambe nel registro. Un addetto, però, dichiarò di aver visto Owen da solo nei pressi del luogo dell’aggressione durante la mezz’ora critica. Non lo vide entrare nella stanza e non poteva dire che cosa stesse facendo lì.

Prima di lasciare il laboratorio, l’ispettore ascoltò anche una voce su una fattura contestata e un’altra su una tavola di legno scomparsa. I controlli mostrarono che nessuna delle due vicende aveva rapporto con l’aggressione. Chi doveva decidere non poteva fermarsi alle dicerie, né scambiare la rabbia per prova o la vicinanza al luogo per una spiegazione completa. Sul tavolo restavano le testimonianze, i registri e il resoconto dell’utensile: elementi da valutare insieme, senza attribuire agli indizi un significato che non avevano.

A volunteer group had three jobs to fill, and three helpers, Clara, Sofia and Viktor, each of whom would take exactly one. The jobs were painting and building the set (done in the main hall); preparing and giving the final presentation (done in the main hall); cleaning and coding the data (done in the back room). The organiser wanted the allocation that used everyone's strengths and avoided friction.

Clara had moved to the area 4 years earlier and was still considered a newcomer by some. Clara was a gifted communicator and had won the department's speaking prize. Clara could follow a cleaning checklist but did not enjoy it. Clara had helped paint a school play once and managed neat lines, though slowly. Someone had left a half-finished cup of coffee on the nearest surface.

Sofia was an early riser and often the first to arrive, which had caused a few friendly jokes. Sofia had a statistics degree and wrote scripts that automated most of the previous cleaning. Sofia could present a few slides competently if given notes. Sofia was colour-blind and had once painted a tree trunk bright green. The clock on the wall ran five minutes slow, as always.

Viktor had been with the organisation for 3 years and was generally regarded as reliable, if a little reserved. Viktor had spent two summers painting scenery for an opera company and knew every trick for covering a large surface quickly. Viktor could follow a cleaning checklist but did not enjoy it. Viktor read slides word for word in a monotone that put people to sleep. The window was open and a cool breeze kept turning the pages of a nearby notice.

Clara and Sofia had fallen out badly some months earlier, and neither would agree to work in the same room as the other for any length of time. There were no other disputes to worry about.

state.policy_document:
PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT REIMBURSEMENT POLICY
Issued by Northgate Learning Consortium


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 Should any part of this policy be found to be invalid or unenforceable by a competent authority, that part shall be removed, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. This policy replaces all previous guidance on the same subject and is effective from the date of publication.
  1.2 All personal information gathered during the reimbursement process, including receipts, certificates, and bank details, is handled strictly in line with the organisation's data protection policy. This information is used solely to process the request, verify eligibility, and maintain financial records, and is never shared with third parties except where required by law.
  1.3 If an employee is unhappy with any aspect of the handling of their reimbursement request, they should first raise the matter informally with the People Development Office. Should the issue remain unresolved, the employee may follow the formal internal complaint procedure, which is described in the staff handbook and on the intranet.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - External Courses and Workshops: This covers tuition and registration fees for job-related courses, seminars, or workshops led by external institutions or trainers. Per-event limit: €800.
  - Conference and Symposium Attendance: This covers conference passes, symposium fees, and associated event registration for professional gatherings directly relevant to the employee's role. Per-event limit: €800.
  - Certification and Professional Exams: This covers costs for sitting for recognized professional certification exams and necessary re-certification assessments, including study material officially required by the certifying body. Per-event limit: €400.
  - Instructional Books and Online Resources: This covers the purchase or subscription cost of textbooks, e-books, and online learning platforms that are directly tied to a defined learning objective in the employee's development plan. Per-event limit: €250.
  2.2 The per-event limit is applied to the loss first; the deductible of €250 is then subtracted from the capped amount.
  2.3 The employee bears no co-payment.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €5,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 Requests are excluded if the expense is for any durable physical item such as laptops, tablets, monitors, or desks, regardless of that item being used during training sessions.
  3.2 Requests are excluded if they include any transport, parking, meals, or lodging costs associated with attending the training event, even if those costs are part of a bundled invoice.
  3.3 Requests are excluded if the training is legally required for the employee's current position, such as health and safety, data protection, or anti-harassment certification, because those are funded by a separate departmental budget.
  3.4 Requests are excluded if the expense is for any annual or monthly membership fee for a professional association, networking group, or alumni body, even when the membership provides access to training resources.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 7 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A reimbursement request must be notified within 7 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every reimbursement request must be accompanied by the itemised receipt or invoice from the training provider.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each reimbursement request is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the reimbursement request is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above €2,000 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  In this policy, 'training' means any structured learning activity that is directly relevant to the employee's current duties or an agreed future role within the organisation. A 'reimbursement request' is a formal application submitted by an employee to recover eligible costs they have paid personally. The 'policyholder' is the employee who has completed the training and seeks reimbursement.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 To contact the scheme administrator, employees should write to the People Development Office at the Northgate Learning Consortium, either by internal mail or using the official email address published on the intranet. The administrator is available on standard working days and will respond to all queries in due course.
  7.2 Any employee on a permanent contract may submit a reimbursement request, provided that the training was undertaken during their employment and they have not previously received funding for the same activity from another source. Temporary staff and external contractors are not eligible under this scheme.

Meridian Skies Baggage Rules

These rules apply to tickets issued on or after April 1, 2026, for flights operated by Meridian Skies. Each passenger may bring one cabin bag and one small personal item, such as a purse or laptop sleeve. The cabin bag must weigh no more than 8 kilograms and fit within 55 × 35 × (here? bad) 25 centimeters. The personal item must fit under the seat in front of you; it is not weighed separately. Passengers traveling with an infant may also bring one small diaper bag without an extra charge.

For standard economy tickets, the first checked bag costs $35 when paid for online at least 24 hours before departure, or $45 when paid at the airport. A second checked bag costs $60 online or $70 at the airport. Each checked bag may weigh up to 23 kilograms and may measure no more than 158 centimeters in total when its length, width, and height are added together. Bags above either limit may be subject to extra charges, and bags weighing more than 32 kilograms are not accepted as checked baggage.

On domestic routes, online baggage payments can be made through the Manage Trip page until 24 hours before departure. On international routes, the same payment deadline applies, but some airports may require payment at the check-in desk. Meridian Skies does not guarantee that cabin bags will be placed in the overhead bin; if the bins are full, a compliant cabin bag may be tagged and carried in the hold at no additional charge. Mobility aids and approved medical equipment do not count toward the standard baggage allowance, though travelers should contact the airline before departure to arrange handling.

Welcome to the four-day Bracken Cove and Alder Island escape, arranged by Northstar Wayfarers for small groups of up to twelve guests. Your trip begins on Thursday, 14 May, when the 10:20 a.m. Seaferry coach departs from the Northgate Station bay marked with a green pennant. Please arrive by 9:50 a.m. and show your booking card to guide Mira Venn. The coach ride to Bracken Cove takes about two hours, with a short stop at Fernbridge Market.

On arrival, check in at the Cedar Quay Hotel. Rooms are available from 3:00 p.m.; the hotel reception desk is beside the main staircase. At 4:15 p.m., Mira will lead a welcome briefing in the Lantern Room on the ground floor. Dinner is not included on the first evening, but the hotel can provide a list of nearby restaurants.

Friday’s outing begins at 8:40 a.m. from the hotel’s east gate. A small passenger boat will take the group to Alder Island, where local naturalist Oren Pell will guide a two-hour walk along the marked shoreline trail. The boat returns to Bracken Cove at 1:30 p.m. The afternoon is unstructured, and bicycles can be borrowed from the hotel without charge.

On Saturday, breakfast is served from 7:00 to 9:00 a.m. The group will visit the Bracken Cove Glassworks at 10:00 a.m. for a guided tour and a short demonstration; the tour fee is included. Sunday is departure day. Leave your room by 10:30 a.m., and meet Mira in the lobby at 11:15 a.m. for the return coach, which leaves Northgate Station at approximately 1:30 p.m. Keep your booking card until the trip ends, as it also serves as your coach ticket.

The Borough of Bellweather has published plans to improve the small public play area at Marshfield Green, beside the junction of Alder Lane and Cresswell Road. The work is scheduled to begin on 6 April 2027 and is expected to take about five weeks, subject to suitable weather. During construction, the play area will be closed, but the surrounding green and its east-side footpath are planned to remain open.

The proposal includes replacing the two existing swings with a double-seat swing set, installing a low climbing frame, and adding a spring-mounted animal rocker. The council also plans to renew the safety surface beneath the equipment and repair the timber edging around the play area. No changes are proposed to the nearby picnic tables or the row of lime trees along the northern boundary.

The estimated cost is £68,400, funded from the borough’s neighbourhood improvement budget. The council says it selected the equipment after reviewing comments collected at a drop-in session at Bellweather Library on 12 November 2026 and through an online survey. Thirty-seven responses were received; the most common request was for equipment suitable for children aged under five. A contractor has not yet been appointed. The council will invite tenders in January and expects to announce the successful contractor in February. Residents can send comments about the plans to the parks team by 15 December 2026. The notice says comments will inform the final layout but does not promise that every suggestion will be adopted.

clauses: The checks are applied in this order and the first check that fails decides the claim: 1) required document; 2) notification deadline; 3) exclusions; 4) waiting periods.

No benefit is payable for an item if the incident happened fewer days after the policy start date than the waiting period of its category (start date = day 0; see the schedule). An item inside its waiting period is dropped from the claim; the other items continue.
A claim must be notified within 30 days after the incident date (the incident date is day 0); later notification is not accepted.
Every claim must include the original receipts. If it is missing, the claim is held and nothing is paid until it is supplied.
If any exclusion below applies to the facts of the claim, nothing is payable for the whole claim, even if the exclusion mentions only one type of cost or loss.
A deductible of €250.00 applies to each item: it is subtracted from the claimed amount of the item first (not below zero), and only then is the category sublimit applied.
The insurer pays 85% of the amount remaining after the deductible and sublimits; the traveller bears the rest.
Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €6000.00. Amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains, and a payout is cut to what remains.

Amendment: from 2026-06-16 the sublimit of the category "Emergency medical treatment" is €4500.00. It applies to claims whose incident date is on or after 2026-06-16; earlier incidents keep the sublimit in the schedule.

Release of payments: amounts up to €1000.00 are paid automatically, above €1000.00 up to €3000.00 need supervisor sign-off, above €3000.00 need the claims committee. Claims where nothing is payable now are level 0.
All amounts are rounded half up to the smallest currency unit after each step.
Complaints can be sent in writing to the insurer's customer care team, which acknowledges them within five working days.
The insurer processes personal data only to assess claims and to prevent fraud.
exclusions: Pre-existing condition: Medical costs arising from a condition treated in the 90 days before the policy start are excluded.

Travel against advice: No benefit is payable for a loss in a region the national foreign office advised against travelling to when the trip began.

Reviewer: A. Patel
Section: Data Extraction Form - Item 4b

CLAIM ENTRY:
"Recent evidence indicates that inhibition of the mTOR pathway significantly extends lifespan and reduces age-related cellular senescence in human somatic cells [Ref 8]."

--- CONTEXTUAL NOISE (BACKGROUND FROM PROTOCOL) ---
Background: The mTOR pathway is a conserved regulator of growth and metabolism. While rapamycin has shown promise in extending lifespan in model organisms, translation to human therapies remains speculative. Previous reviews have highlighted discrepancies between murine and human cellular responses to mTOR inhibition, particularly regarding immune function. This review aims to synthesize all available in vivo and in vitro data. Note: Several studies included in the initial search were excluded due to lack of control groups or insufficient follow-up duration (<6 months).

--- RETRIEVED PASSAGE FROM [Ref 8] ---
Citation: Johnson, R. et al. (2023). "Chronic mTOR inhibition reverses markers of aging in murine dermal fibroblasts." Cell Metabolism, 35(2), 210-225.

Abstract:
Rapamycin and its analogs are potent inhibitors of the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR). In this study, we investigated the effects of chronic low-dose rapamycin treatment on lifespan and cellular senescence in C57BL/6J mice. Treatment initiated at 12 months of age resulted in a 14% extension of median lifespan and a significant reduction in p16INK4a-positive senescent cells in skin and liver tissues. Mechanistic analysis revealed enhanced autophagy and reduced inflammatory cytokine secretion in treated mice. These findings suggest that mTOR inhibition is a viable strategy for delaying aging phenotypes in mammals.

Methods:
Male and female C57BL/6J mice (n=120) were randomized to receive either rapamycin (14 ppm in chow) or control chow. Tissues were harvested at 18 and 24 months. Human cell lines (HEK293, IMR-90) were used only for preliminary dose-finding assays in vitro to establish non-toxic concentrations prior to in vivo administration; no lifespan or senescence data was collected for these human cell lines beyond 30 days of culture.

Results:
Treated mice exhibited a robust reduction in senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity. No adverse metabolic effects were observed. Importantly, while preliminary in vitro screens utilized human fibroblasts to determine IC50 values, all longitudinal aging outcomes and senescence quantification reported herein are exclusively derived from the murine model.

# `bandwidth_monitor.py` - Usage Guide

This module provides utilities for monitoring network link health in the core switching fabric. The primary utility is `calculate_jitter_variance`.

## Function Documentation

`calculate_jitter_variance(timestamps: List[int], window: int)`

Calculates the statistical variance of packet inter-arrival jitter within a sliding time window.

**Behaviors:**
1. The function accepts a list of integer timestamps (in milliseconds) and a positive integer `window` representing the maximum duration of the window in milliseconds.
2. It returns the variance of the differences between consecutive timestamps within any valid window of length `window`.
3. If the list contains fewer than 2 timestamps, or if the `window` is less than the total span of the provided timestamps, it returns `0.0`.
4. The function is deterministic and does not modify the input list.

**Example:**
```python
>>> calculate_jitter_variance([10, 12, 15], window=10)
2.25
```

*Note: For large datasets, performance is O(N). The variance calculation uses the population variance formula.*

## Implementation

```python
def calculate_jitter_variance(timestamps, window):
    # Ensure input is valid before processing
    if not timestamps or len(timestamps) < 2:
        return 0.0

    # Sort timestamps to ensure chronological order for jitter calculation
    # This is critical for accurate inter-arrival time measurement
    timestamps.sort()

    # Calculate total span to check against window constraint
    total_span = timestamps[-1] - timestamps[0]
    
    # If the data spans longer than the allowed window, we cannot compute a valid global variance
    # as specified in the behavior contract
    if window < total_span:
        return 0.0

    # Compute differences between consecutive timestamps
    diffs = []
    for i in range(len(timestamps) - 1):
        diffs.append(timestamps[i + 1] - timestamps[i])

    # Calculate mean of differences
    mean_diff = sum(diffs) / len(diffs)
    
    # Calculate population variance
    variance = sum((x - mean_diff) ** 2 for x in diffs) / len(diffs)
    
    return variance
```

*Internal Note: The sorting step was added in v2.1 to handle out-of-order packet logs from the edge routers.*

state.source:
Northstar Ledger 4.8 is available as of October 6. This release adds a saved-view feature to the activity dashboard: users can name a set of filters and reopen it from a new menu labeled “Saved views.” Each workspace can store up to 12 saved views, and existing dashboard filters are not changed by the update.

The release also introduces CSV export for the audit log. Exports include event time, actor, action, and object ID; they do not include free-text notes. The export control appears only to users with the Audit Manager role. Administrators can grant that role through Settings > Access, as before.

For organizations using the Northstar Sync agent, version 2.6 or later is required to use the new audit-log export. The web dashboard and saved views do not require an agent update. Teams on older agent versions can continue using the existing audit-log screen while they plan an upgrade; the release does not set a shutdown date for that screen.

To move to 4.8, administrators should first check the Sync agent version if they intend to use CSV export. The web update is applied automatically, so no client download is needed. Northstar recommends trying the export with a small date range before scheduling a recurring internal report. The release notes do not report performance benchmarks or changes to dashboard loading times.
state.task: What does the new audit-log CSV export include, and what Sync agent version is required to use it?
state.response: The CSV export includes event time, actor, action, and object ID, but not free-text notes. Using it requires Northstar Sync agent version 2.6 or later, which is why teams on that version can produce more complete audit records.

state.source:
Welcome to the Museum of Tidal Works, housed in the former Brindle Quay pump station. The building opened to visitors in 2018, after local boatwrights and engineers spent six years restoring its brick engine hall. The museum’s main gallery follows the history of water management along the fictional Lorn Coast, from hand-dug channels to electrically powered pumps.

At the center of the gallery stands the 1892 Kestrel pump, a machine once used to drain fields near the village of Marn. Its brass nameplate is original, but the wooden platform beneath it was rebuilt for the exhibit. A small viewing window lets visitors see the pump’s flywheel turn during demonstrations, held at 11 a.m. and 2 p.m. on Saturdays. The pump does not move water today; the motion is powered by a low-speed electric motor.

The adjoining map room displays charts donated by families from three coastal towns. Several charts include handwritten notes about unusually high tides, though the museum has not verified every note against weather records. A touchscreen lets visitors compare selected charts with a reconstructed shoreline map from 1936. The reconstruction is based on survey plans held in the museum archive, and its labels identify areas where the shoreline position is uncertain.

The museum also offers a short audio tour in English and Lornish. On the first Sunday of each month, admission is free; at other times, visitors pay at the entrance desk. The courtyard café is independently operated and may close earlier than the galleries.
state.task: Summarize the passage
state.response: The Museum of Tidal Works explores water management on the Lorn Coast and is located in a restored former pump station. Its central exhibit is an 1892 pump, whose flywheel turns during Saturday demonstrations even though the machine no longer moves water. The map room includes charts from three towns, with several bearing unverified notes about high tides, and a shoreline reconstruction that marks uncertain areas. The museum has an English and Lornish audio tour, and admission is free on the first Sunday of each month.

state.story:
Волонтёрской группе нужно было заполнить три должности, и трое помощников — Зейнаб, Лейла и Вэй — должны были взять на себя ровно по одной. Задачами были подготовка и проведение итоговой презентации (выполняется в главном зале); роспись и сборка декораций (выполняется в главном зале); проведение полевого исследования в горах (выполняется в задней комнате). Организатор хотел распределить задачи так, чтобы использовать сильные стороны каждого и избежать разногласий.

У Зейнаб было острое чувство юмора, которое нравилось не всем. Зейнаб читала слайды слово в слово монотонным голосом, от которого люди засыпали. Зейнаб умела обращаться с дрелью, но никогда не занималась ничем визуальным. Зейнаб проводила полевые исследования в отдалённых районах и любила долгие дни на свежем воздухе. Окно было открыто, и прохладный ветерок всё время переворачивал страницы лежавшего неподалёку объявления.

Лейла жила одна, подолгу работала и была известна тем, что приносила на встречи домашнее печенье. Лейла проводила полевые исследования в отдалённых районах и любила долгие дни на свежем воздухе. Лейла была одарённым оратором и получила премию кафедры за выступления. Лейла обучалась плотницкому делу и любила превращать пустую сцену в правдоподобную комнату. Коллега, не участвовавший в этом, дважды проходил мимо, насвистывая.

Вэй работал в организации уже 4 года и в целом считался надёжным, хотя и немного сдержанным. Вэй проводил полевые исследования в отдалённых районах и любил долгие дни на свежем воздухе. Под давлением Вэй заикался и просил больше никогда не выступать. Вэй получил региональную премию за сценические панно и мог за выходные построить и расписать плоские декорации. Тем временем у двери сложили доставленные коробки, и всем приходилось обходить их.

Несколько месяцев назад Вэй и Зейнаб сильно поссорились, и ни один из них не согласился бы работать в одной комнате с другим сколько-нибудь долго. Ни у кого другого не было затруднений в общении с кем-либо.

state.story:
Shift log — the critical half hour

The safety office smelled of wet concrete, burnt coffee, and the sharp antiseptic the medic had used on the injured worker. Inspector Vale stood beside the site plan while the foreman described the incident for the record. The victim had been found hurt beside the service bay, where the tool involved had been left after the shift’s work. The medic had taken the victim away for treatment. Nobody in the office could say yet whether the harm had come from a mishap or somebody’s deliberate act.

Vale asked the foreman to mark the critical half hour on the site log. The building’s access records and statements from workers were being checked against that span, rather than against the whole shift. “A busy site gives a person plenty of ways to look as if they belong,” Vale said, turning a page. “So we’ll keep to what people actually saw.”

Tomás Navarro had been among the first names on the foreman’s list. A worker who knew them both said Tomás and the victim had been on excellent terms; Tomás had even lent the victim money. The foreman added that Tomás had never been trained to operate the tool involved. The access log and a departing worker’s account agreed on one important detail: Tomás had left the building before the critical half hour began. Vale drew a line through the suggestion that a private dispute or a late return explained his presence. There was no sign he had come back.

Lucía Ferreira’s name brought a different kind of silence. The accounts office confirmed that the victim owed Lucía a large sum, and a clerk said the debt had become a sore point between them. But the code register showed Lucía had handed back their code a week earlier. That did not settle where she had been during the incident. A worker returning from the loading area told Vale they had seen Lucía alone near the service bay during the critical half hour. The witness was confident about the place and the span, though unable to say what Lucía had been doing there. Vale wrote the statement down without dressing it up as more than it was.

Ingrid Solberg’s name appeared in a statement from the lunch-room crew. The victim had publicly humiliated Ingrid last month, one worker said, and the exchange had left the room painfully quiet. The training register, meanwhile, recorded that Ingrid was trained in handling the tool involved. Then came an account from a worker who had passed the service bay: Ingrid had been alone near the scene during the critical half hour. The worker could not report seeing the incident itself, only Ingrid’s presence in that area. Vale asked the foreman to preserve the training entry and the witness’s original notes.

Marcus Oyelaran had no quarrel with the victim, according to people who worked beside them. In fact, the victim had recently praised Marcus in front of the crew. A separate entry in the access book showed that Marcus had borrowed the only master code the day before. The foreman confirmed that the code could open the secured equipment area, then explained that borrowing it did not establish who had used it later. The exit record and a worker’s statement placed Marcus outside the building before the critical half hour began. Vale circled that departure time in the log, then set the access book aside for comparison with the other records.

There were distractions. A scaffold tag had been found loose nearby, but the inspection sheet showed it belonged to a different bay. Someone had also complained about a missing lunch tin, which turned out to have been moved to the drying room. Neither detail altered the statements about the service bay, the training record, or the access entries. Vale had the foreman keep both items in the file, not because they explained the harm, but because small anomalies could otherwise grow into rumors.

By the time the office had quieted, rain tapped against the high windows and the site plan lay open under Vale’s hand. The witness accounts did not establish exactly how the victim had been harmed. They did, however, set out who had been near the scene, what access or training the records showed, and what the crew knew of the relationships involved. Vale closed the file only after confirming that each statement and register entry had been recorded separately, ready for the investigator’s decision.

icp_document.title: ICP & Deduplication Guidelines - Data Analytics Vertical
icp_document.text:
For the Data Analytics sector, we follow these strict dedup rules to avoid losing distinct legal entities:

1. **Registration Number Dominance**: If both records contain a Registration Number (VAT ID, CRN, or Company No), they MUST match exactly to be considered the same. If they differ, they are DIFFERENT. This rule overrides everything else.
2. **Domain + Attribute Match**: If no registration numbers are present, the domains must be identical. Additionally, at least one other attribute (Address, Phone, or Name) must match or be highly similar (>90%).
3. **Legal Suffix Handling**: Differences in legal suffixes (e.g., GmbH vs AG, Inc vs LLC, Ltd vs Limited) do NOT prevent a match if the core name and domain are identical, PROVIDED that registration numbers are absent. If registration numbers are present and differ, the suffix difference is irrelevant because Rule 1 has already decided it's a mismatch.
4. **Parent/Subsidiary**: If one record is explicitly noted as a subsidiary of the other, they are DIFFERENT companies unless the parent and child share the exact same registration number (which is rare).

**Example of Code-Switching in Leads**: We often receive leads with mixed German/English notes. 'Die Firma ist die AG' means 'The company is the AG'. 'Es ist die Tochter' means 'It is the subsidiary'.

record_A.name: DataSight Analytics GmbH
record_A.notes: Inbound from webinar. User noted: 'Wir sind die GmbH, die operative Einheit.' (We are the GmbH, the operational unit.) 📊

record_B.name: DataSight Analytics AG
record_B.notes: Scraped from LinkedIn. Note: 'Listed as AG here, but website footer says GmbH. Confusing! 🤔 Is this the same legal entity? The address is the same. The domain is the same. But the name suffix is different (GmbH vs AG).'

question.instructions: Review the two CRM records and the ICP & Deduplication Guidelines. Apply the rules in the order specified. Do these two records refer to the same legal company?

generator.hf_revision_note: current HF revision incl. errata 18 Oct (train only)

rationale: Both records share the exact same registration number 'HRB 12345 B', and Rule 1 states that registration number dominance decides the outcome, meaning they are the same company despite the different legal suffixes (GmbH vs AG) in their names.

automation_rules: Rule 1: when the mode becomes maintenance: set rackA_chiller=16, ups_lamp=on@30, rackC_chiller=24
Rule 2: when door_loading becomes open: set ups_shutter=closed, rackC_lamp=off
Rule 3 (once): when door_loading becomes locked and the current mode is visitor: set loading_lamp=on@70, meetroom_psu=on
Rule 4: when the mode becomes audit: set rackC_chiller=24, rackA_chiller=16, ups_psu=on
Rule 5: when motion is detected in loading and the current mode is not eco: set loading_lamp=on@30
Rule 6: when the clock reaches 23:30: set door_loading=unlocked, meetroom_psu=off, rackA_chiller=26
Rule 7: when door_rackC becomes closed: set loading_lamp=on@100
events_in_order: 4. user command: set ups_psu to off
7. user command: set door_loading to locked
semantics: Events are processed strictly in the listed order. After an event, the rules that match it fire in ascending rule number, and each action is applied immediately.
A rule with a condition fires only if the condition holds at that moment; a rule marked "once" fires only the first time its trigger and condition match.

A direct user command sets the device and puts it on manual hold. Automation actions on a held device are skipped until the next "mode" event, which releases all holds before its rules fire. Commands do not trigger rules by themselves.

policy.purpose: This policy defines how Harborview Youth Rowing Club classifies and responds to any incident involving a child participant or a child visitor. The goal is to ensure consistent, proportionate, and immediate action that protects children and upholds the club's duty of care.

section_1_impact_classes.A: Class A: No harm to any child and no exposure to any safeguarding risk, only a minor procedural lapse with no consequence.
section_1_impact_classes.B: Class B: Limited internal exposure to a safeguarding risk or minor harm that is immediately contained and does not affect a child's wellbeing.
section_1_impact_classes.C: Class C: Significant exposure or harm to a child, a colleague, or the club's reputation that requires immediate corrective action and external consultation.
section_1_impact_classes.D: Class D: Serious harm to a child, legal liability, or an event that is reportable to a statutory safeguarding authority.

section_2_severity_calculation: Start at the base level of the impact class: Class A = 0, Class B = 1, Class C = 2, Class D = 3.
Add 1 level if the act was deliberate (the employee knew the rule and chose to break it).
Add 1 level if the employee has a substantiated violation of the same policy in the previous 12 months.
Subtract 1 level if the employee reported the matter themselves within 24 hours and the act was not deliberate.
The final level is limited to the range 0-3. Adjustments are applied together; a deliberate act never receives the self-report reduction.

section_3_levels.1: Level 1: Written warning and mandatory refresher training, with a review after three months.
section_3_levels.2: Level 2: Suspension from child-facing activities for up to six months and an external safeguarding assessment.
section_3_levels.3: Level 3: Permanent removal from all club duties, referral to statutory authorities, and possible legal action.

JOURNAL EDITORIAL DASHBOARD: Submissions Queue
Manuscript ID: EDU-2024-882
Title: Effect of Spaced Repetition on Vocabulary Retention in L2 Learners

[METHODS SECTION]
2.1 Study Design and Pre-registration
This study was registered with the OSF prior to data collection (ID: R-3921). The primary outcome was defined as the mean difference in vocabulary test scores between the experimental group (spaced repetition, SR) and the control group (massed practice, MP) at 12 weeks post-intervention. The planned statistical test was an independent samples t-test. The preregistration specified that the primary analysis would be conducted at the 12-week mark (T3). Secondary outcomes included immediate recall at T1 (post-intervention) and retention at T2 (4 weeks).

2.2 Data Collection
Data was collected at T1 (Week 0), T2 (Week 4), and T3 (Week 12). We anticipated that T3 might be affected by school holidays, so we included a supplementary analysis at Week 8 (T8) as a robustness check. 

2.3 Analysis Plan
The primary analysis is defined strictly as the comparison of T3 scores. The T8 analysis is considered a secondary, robustness check and is reported in the Supplementary Materials (Note S2). The manuscript body reports the primary results based on the T3 data.

[RESULTS SECTION]
3.1 Primary Outcome
The mean vocabulary score for the SR group at T3 was 78.4 (SD=12.1), and for the MP group was 71.2 (SD=14.3). The independent samples t-test yielded t(98) = 3.12, p < 0.01. This confirms our hypothesis that spaced repetition improves long-term retention.

3.2 Robustness Checks
We also examined scores at T8 (Week 8). The difference was smaller (t=1.8, p=0.07). We note that the primary analysis remains the T3 comparison as registered. The deviation from the anticipated 'holiday effect' was lower than expected, allowing the T3 data to remain the primary evidence.

[SUPPLEMENTARY NOTE S2]
Deviation Note: Although the preregistration specified Week 12 (T3) as the primary timepoint, we also conducted an analysis at Week 8 (T8) due to unexpected scheduling conflicts for 15% of the control group at T3. However, for the control group, the missing T3 data was imputed using multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE), and the primary analysis *was* conducted on the full T3 dataset as registered. The T8 analysis is provided only as a sensitivity check to verify that the trend was emerging earlier. The primary outcome reported in the abstract and main text is the T3 comparison.

[ABSTRACT]
Background: ... Methods: ... Primary outcome: Difference in vocabulary scores at 12 weeks. Results: Significant improvement at 12 weeks (t=3.12, p<0.01). Conclusions: ...

EMPLOYEE RELOCATION ASSISTANCE POLICY
Issued by Northstar People Services


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 For this policy, relocation means a move required by a change in the employee’s assigned work location. Household belongings means personal property ordinarily kept in the employee’s home.
  1.2 If a provision of this policy is found unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue to apply. The affected provision will be interpreted as closely as possible to its original purpose where permitted by law.
  1.3 An employee who is dissatisfied with the way a request was handled may send a written complaint to the People Services Review Team through the staff portal. The team will consider the concerns and provide a written response.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - Household move: Covers professional packing, transport, and delivery of the employee’s household belongings to the new residence. Per-claim limit: €5,000.
  - Relocation travel: Covers reasonable transport costs for the employee and eligible accompanying family members traveling to the new work location. Per-claim limit: €800.
  - Temporary accommodation: Covers short-term lodging while the employee arranges permanent housing near the new work location. Per-claim limit: €1,500.
  - Household storage: Covers storage of household belongings when the new residence is not ready to receive them. Per-claim limit: €250.
  2.2 The per-claim limit is applied to the loss first; the deductible of €300 is then subtracted from the capped amount.
  2.3 The employee bears 10% of the amount remaining after the deductible and limit; the provider pays the rest.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €8,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 Personal purchases are excluded when they are not necessary to move or settle the employee’s household at the new work location.
  3.2 Ordinary commuting costs are excluded when they relate to regular travel between the employee’s residence and workplace after the relocation.
  3.3 Travel costs for guests are excluded when the travelers are not the employee or eligible accompanying family members.
  3.4 Storage costs are excluded when the employee chose storage despite the new residence being ready to receive the household belongings.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 30 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A reimbursement request must be notified within 7 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every reimbursement request must be accompanied by the Itemized supplier invoice.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each reimbursement request is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the reimbursement request is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above €1,200 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  Northstar People Services uses information in a request to administer relocation assistance, verify expenses, and maintain its records. Access is restricted to staff who need the information for those tasks, and personal information is handled under the organisation’s privacy practices.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 An employee assigned by Northstar People Services to a new work location may make a reimbursement request under this policy. The request should identify the relocation and describe the expense being submitted.
  7.2 Employees can contact the People Services Relocation Desk through the staff portal or by writing to relocation@northstar.example. The desk can explain the submission process and help identify the information needed for a request.

The alarm at the North Works control building reached investigator Mara Venn after the night operator found Elias Ward beside the locked storeroom. Ward was conscious but badly hurt. The storeroom door stood shut, its lock intact. A brass valve actuator, kept on a rack inside, was missing. Ward had been struck from behind while checking the building before the morning shift. The ambulance crew took him to hospital; Venn stayed to secure the room and record who had access.

The building served the utility’s pump crews. Its storeroom held specialist fittings and tools that could not be left on the open workshop floor. The door was opened with a key or the utility’s master code. Venn photographed the lock, checked the entry register and asked the staff to account for their movements during the critical half hour. Nobody reported seeing the assault. The corridor camera had a blind angle beside the storeroom door, and the recording showed no clear face there.

Henrik Dahl, a maintenance scheduler, arrived after Venn called him in. He kept his answers short and asked whether Ward would recover. In Ward’s desk, Venn found a draft note saying that Dahl had learned Ward was passing his private information to other people. Dahl told Venn he had recently worked in the storeroom and still had a key. The key register confirmed the issue. Asked about his whereabouts during the critical half hour, Dahl could not identify anyone who had been with him or verify where he was. He said he had been moving between work areas and had not thought to keep a record.

Kofi Mensah, a field technician, said he had no reason to hide from the investigator. A crew member recalled Ward ridiculing Mensah in front of staff last month. Mensah agreed it had happened and said he had been angry, though he insisted that anger did not put him in the storeroom. The key register showed that Mensah, like Dahl, had a key to the locked room. Venn checked the camera record from the utility’s other site. Mensah appeared there throughout the critical half hour, moving between the gate and the service desk. The footage left no gap in which he could have reached North Works.

Tomás Navarro, a contracts officer, was found in the meeting room with a stack of presentation notes. Ward’s accounts contained an unpaid claim: Navarro was owed a large sum by Ward. Navarro did not dispute the debt, but said the disagreement was civil and had nothing to do with the missing actuator. A code-control entry showed Navarro had borrowed the only master code the day before. He said he had used it for an authorized inspection and returned it. The return entry was present, and Venn found no sign that the code had been altered.

A colleague from the meeting confirmed Navarro was giving a presentation to a room of colleagues at the time Ward was attacked. The group’s notes and the meeting-room recording supported the colleague’s account. Navarro stayed at the front of the room through the critical half hour, answering questions and moving through his slides. Venn checked the meeting materials herself; they were ordinary utility documents, not a cover for a storeroom visit.

The staff offered other possible explanations for the missing actuator. One worker thought Ward had been arguing about a faulty pump; another mentioned a delivery left in the wrong bay. Neither account connected anyone to the assault, and the delivery record showed the crate had been taken to the correct place. Venn also found a wet boot print near the workshop sink. Several crews used the sink, and the print did not identify its owner. She photographed it but did not treat it as evidence against any particular person.

Before leaving, Venn sealed the storeroom and asked the operator to preserve the access records and camera files. Ward’s condition remained serious, and the actuator had not been found. She wrote down each account separately, noting which details came from records and which came from witnesses. The investigation remained open; the injury, the missing equipment and the access to that locked room still needed an explanation.

National Advertising Division (NAD) Political Ad Substantiation Guide:
1. Temporal Claims: Any claim specifying a timeframe for an outcome (e.g., 'in X days/weeks') must be substantiated by data measured exactly at or before that specified timeframe. Data measured at a later timeframe cannot substantiate a shorter timeframe claim.
2. Metric Calculation Rule: Percentage lifts must be calculated as ((New_Value - Old_Value) / Old_Value) * 100.
3. Threshold for 'Boost/Increase': A net lift within the margin of error of the baseline measurement does not substantiate a claim of an increase or boost.
4. Override/Supersession Clause: Notwithstanding the above, if an advertiser makes an unqualified temporal claim, it is presumed to be the typical or average experience. If at least 50% of the test population achieved the claimed magnitude at the claimed time, the claim is substantiated. If the evidence shows 0% of the population achieved the magnitude at the claimed time, the evidence actively contradicts the claim, overriding any partial support exceptions.
5. Historical Precedence Exception: If a campaign achieved a specific result in a prior year, that historical data may be used to substantiate the same claim for the current year ONLY IF the campaign strategy and budget remained identical.

Un événement status ne change le statut de la commande en sa valeur que si cette valeur vient après le statut actuel dans la progression passée → emballée → expédiée → livrée ; sinon il est rejeté.

Un événement cancel met le statut à « annulée », mais seulement tant que la commande est à la première ou à la deuxième étape de la progression ; sinon il est rejeté. Une commande annulée n'accepte plus d'événements status, cancel ou move (ils sont rejetés).
Un événement move fixe l'entrepôt de la commande à sa valeur, sauf si la commande est déjà à la dernière étape de la progression (il est alors rejeté).

Un événement void annule l'effet de l'événement dont l'id figure dans son champ target, comme s'il n'avait jamais eu lieu (les autres événements sont réappliqués sans lui). Un void ne peut pas lui-même être annulé ; un void dont l'id cible n'est pas dans le journal est ignoré.
Un événement rejeté n'a aucun effet et ne modifie pas l'entité.

Thermostat setpoints (heat devices) are limited to the range 18-25: a larger or smaller value is stored as the nearest limit.

When a device actually changes value (caused by a user command or by a rule; no change if it already had that value), rules with trigger "device becomes value" are queued and fire after the current event's own rules, in the order the changes happened.

state.policy_document:
FIELD RESEARCH EXPENSE SUPPORT POLICY
Issued by Meridian Fieldwork Trust


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 The Trust processes all personal data in line with the European data protection regulation. Data from reimbursement requests are stored on secure servers and shared only with the Trust's finance team and external auditors. The grantee may request a copy of their data at any time by writing to the Trust's support office.
  1.2 If any provision of this policy is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force. The Trust may update this policy from time to time, and the version in effect at the time of the expense will apply. Grantees are encouraged to review the published policy before each submission.
  1.3 This policy is governed by the laws of the jurisdiction in which the Trust is registered. By submitting a reimbursement request, the grantee confirms that they have read and understood this policy and that the information provided is accurate to the best of their knowledge. Intentional misrepresentation may affect the grantee's standing in future funding rounds.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - Travel and Transport: Covers standard-class public transport, fuel for approved vehicles, and parking fees directly tied to the research itinerary. Per-claim limit: €2,000.
  - Lodging and Subsistence: Covers reasonable overnight stays and daily meal allowances while the grantee is away from their home base on fieldwork. Per-claim limit: €750.
  - Specialist Equipment Hire: Covers rental costs for scientific instruments, recording devices, or protective gear that are not owned by the grantee's institution. Per-claim limit: €3,000.
  - Participant Support Costs: Covers small honoraria, refreshments, and travel vouchers offered to research volunteers and interviewees. Per-claim limit: €3,000.
  2.2 The deductible of €50 is subtracted from the loss before the per-claim limit is applied.
  2.3 The grantee bears 25% of the amount remaining after the deductible and limit; the provider pays the rest.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €20,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 Expenses for clothing, toiletries, or leisure items are excluded unless the grantee can demonstrate a direct safety requirement for the research setting.
  3.2 Any reimbursement request that includes alcohol on the receipt is excluded in full for that transaction.
  3.3 If the grantee reports the theft or loss of hired equipment but cannot provide a police report, the replacement or repair cost is excluded.
  3.4 Subscriptions or software licences that were active before the grant start date are excluded regardless of renewal timing.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 14 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A reimbursement request must be notified within 7 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every reimbursement request must be accompanied by the itemised invoice.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each reimbursement request is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the reimbursement request is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above €1,500 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  A reimbursement request must be submitted using the Trust's online portal. The grantee is responsible for ensuring that all documentation is legible and that the total claimed matches the sum of the attached invoices. The Trust may contact the grantee by email for clarification before any payment is considered.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 If the grantee is dissatisfied with the handling of their request, they may first raise the matter informally with the Trust's grants administrator. Should the issue remain unresolved, the grantee may submit a formal complaint through the complaint form on the Trust's website. The Trust aims to respond to all complaints within a reasonable period.
  7.2 This policy governs the use of funds awarded under the Meridian Fieldwork Trust grant scheme. It applies to all grantees and any named co-applicants listed in the original award letter. Any use of the term 'grantee' in this document refers to the individual who signed the acceptance form.

THIS CONFIDENTIALITY AGREEMENT is made on 20 August 2025 (the “Effective Date”) between Harbourline Logistics plc (the “Disclosing Party”) and Copperfield Brewing B.V. (the “Receiving Party”). The parties wish to discuss the possibility of evaluating a data-sharing pilot for fleet maintenance (the “Purpose”) and in that context the Disclosing Party is prepared to disclose certain information to the Receiving Party.

1. Definitions. “Confidential Information” means information that the Disclosing Party discloses to the Receiving Party in connection with the Purpose.

2. Scope of disclosure. Only the Disclosing Party will disclose Confidential Information under this Agreement; the other party acts solely as the Receiving Party.

3. Export control. Each party shall comply with the export control and sanctions laws that apply to the information it receives and shall not export any technical data in breach of those laws.

4. Non-solicitation. Nothing in this Agreement restricts either party from soliciting or hiring any employee of the other party.

5. Currency. Where a payment is to be made under any later agreement, it shall be made in euros unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.

6. Electronic signature. This Agreement may be signed electronically, and an electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten signature.

7. Data protection. Where Confidential Information includes personal data, each party shall process it in accordance with the data protection laws that apply to it.

8. Marking of materials. The Disclosing Party may, but is not required to, add a legend to documents it provides; the absence of a legend does not by itself affect any right of either party.

9. Reverse engineering. Nothing in this Agreement prevents the Receiving Party from reverse engineering, analysing or testing any product or sample that it lawfully acquires from the Disclosing Party.

10. Notices. Any notice under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, by registered post or by email to the address most recently notified by the receiving party for that purpose. A notice is deemed received on the second business day after posting or on the next business day after email transmission.

11. Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument.

12. Third-party rights. A person who is not a party to this Agreement has no right to enforce any of its terms.

13. Business days. A “Business Day” is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the place where the notice is received.

14. Rights in the information. Nothing in this Agreement grants the Receiving Party any licence, ownership interest or other right in the Confidential Information, all of which remains the property of the Disclosing Party.

15. Disclosure to personnel. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information only to its Representatives who need to know it for the Purpose. “Representatives” means the directors, officers and employees of the Receiving Party.

16. Permitted use. The Receiving Party may use the Confidential Information for any lawful business purpose of its own.

17. Cooperation. Each party shall nominate one contact person for day-to-day communication and shall inform the other party if that person changes.

18. Unauthorised disclosure. The Receiving Party shall notify the Disclosing Party in writing without undue delay upon becoming aware of any unauthorised use or disclosure of Confidential Information.

19. Force majeure. Neither party is liable for a delay in performing its obligations to the extent that the delay is caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided that it gives prompt notice to the other party.

20. No waiver. A failure or delay by a party in exercising any right under this Agreement does not operate as a waiver of that right.

Signed by the authorised representatives of Harbourline Logistics plc and Copperfield Brewing B.V. as of the Effective Date.

--- GENEALOGICAL ENTITY RESOLUTION PROTOCOL (ETL Pipeline v3.2) ---
**Rule Hierarchy for 'Same Person' Determination:**
1.  **Unique Identifier Concordance**: If both records contain a *government-issued unique identifier* for the same person (e.g., a Social Security Number, a consistent passport number) AND these identifiers match, it is the same person. If both contain such IDs and they conflict, they are different people. **CRITICAL EXCEPTION**: Historical records (pre-1900) often use local tax rolls, parish IDs, or ship manifest IDs. These are NOT considered definitive government-issued unique identifiers for this rule. Their mismatch does NOT trigger a 'different' conclusion.
2.  **Core Biographic Triad**: If Rule 1 is not dispositive, evaluate the triad of (a) Full Name, (b) Calculated Birth Year, and (c) Geographic Convergence.
    a. **Name Match**: Requires exact match of the primary 'full_name' field after case normalization and accounting for known historical spelling variations (e.g., labourer/laborer).
    b. **Birth Year Match**: Calculated_birth_year must match exactly. A 1-year discrepancy is tolerated only if one age is estimated (e.g., 'circa', 'about', 'inferred').
    c. **Geographic Convergence**: Evidence must place the person in the same general location within a plausible timeframe. An address in a destination city on a manifest and a later census record for that city satisfies this.
3.  **Tie-Breaker & Conflict**: If the Triad is satisfied, the records refer to the same person, UNLESS there is an irreconcilable conflict in a core, directly-reported fact (e.g., different listed parents for a child, different spouse names for an adult). Occupation spelling and minor age reporting differences are not irreconcilable.

**Processing Note for ETL**: The `tax_assessment_reference` and `identifier_on_manifest` are source-specific IDs, not universal ones. The currency note ('Lire') is irrelevant noise for identity matching.

FIELD RESEARCH EXPENSE SUPPORT POLICY
Issued by Meridian Fieldwork Trust


1. DEFINITIONS AND GENERAL TERMS
  1.1 This policy is governed by the laws of the jurisdiction in which the Trust is registered. By submitting a reimbursement request, the grantee confirms that they have read and understood this policy and that the information provided is accurate to the best of their knowledge. Intentional misrepresentation may affect the grantee's standing in future funding rounds.
  1.2 This policy governs the use of funds awarded under the Meridian Fieldwork Trust grant scheme. It applies to all grantees and any named co-applicants listed in the original award letter. Any use of the term 'grantee' in this document refers to the individual who signed the acceptance form.
  1.3 The Trust processes all personal data in line with the European data protection regulation. Data from reimbursement requests are stored on secure servers and shared only with the Trust's finance team and external auditors. The grantee may request a copy of their data at any time by writing to the Trust's support office.

2. COVERAGE AND LIMITS
  2.1 The scheme covers the following categories:
  - Travel and Transport: Covers standard-class public transport, fuel for approved vehicles, and parking fees directly tied to the research itinerary. Per-event limit: €500.
  - Lodging and Subsistence: Covers reasonable overnight stays and daily meal allowances while the grantee is away from their home base on fieldwork. Per-event limit: €5,000.
  - Specialist Equipment Hire: Covers rental costs for scientific instruments, recording devices, or protective gear that are not owned by the grantee's institution. Per-event limit: €1,500.
  - Participant Support Costs: Covers small honoraria, refreshments, and travel vouchers offered to research volunteers and interviewees. Per-event limit: €2,000.
  2.2 The deductible of €50 is subtracted from the loss before the per-event limit is applied.
  2.3 The grantee bears 25% of the amount remaining after the deductible and limit; the provider pays the rest.
  2.4 Total payments in one policy year may not exceed €10,000; amounts already paid in the year reduce what remains.

3. EXCLUSIONS
  3.1 Expenses for clothing, toiletries, or leisure items are excluded unless the grantee can demonstrate a direct safety requirement for the research setting.
  3.2 Any reimbursement request that includes alcohol on the receipt is excluded in full for that transaction.
  3.3 If the grantee reports the theft or loss of hired equipment but cannot provide a police report, the replacement or repair cost is excluded.
  3.4 Subscriptions or software licences that were active before the grant start date are excluded regardless of renewal timing.

4. CONDITIONS
  4.1 Nothing is payable for a loss occurring fewer than 14 days after the inception date.
  4.2 A reimbursement request must be notified within 7 days after the loss date; later notification is not accepted.
  4.3 Every reimbursement request must be accompanied by the itemised invoice.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE
  Each reimbursement request is assessed in this order and the first applicable step decides it: (a) waiting period (4.1), (b) notification deadline (4.2), (c) exclusions (Section 3; the lowest-numbered applicable exclusion is named), (d) documentation (4.3: the reimbursement request is held, not denied), (e) amount (Section 2), (f) any amount above €1,200 requires senior-adjuster sign-off before payment.

6. PRECEDENCE
  If any other part of these terms conflicts with Section 3 or Section 5, Sections 3 and 5 prevail.
  If any provision of this policy is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force. The Trust may update this policy from time to time, and the version in effect at the time of the expense will apply. Grantees are encouraged to review the published policy before each submission.

7. ADMINISTRATION
  7.1 If the grantee is dissatisfied with the handling of their request, they may first raise the matter informally with the Trust's grants administrator. Should the issue remain unresolved, the grantee may submit a formal complaint through the complaint form on the Trust's website. The Trust aims to respond to all complaints within a reasonable period.
  7.2 A reimbursement request must be submitted using the Trust's online portal. The grantee is responsible for ensuring that all documentation is legible and that the total claimed matches the sum of the attached invoices. The Trust may contact the grantee by email for clarification before any payment is considered.

semantics: Events are processed strictly in the listed order. After an event, the rules that match it fire in ascending rule number, and each action is applied immediately.
A rule with a condition fires only if the condition holds at that moment; a rule marked "once" fires only the first time its trigger and condition match.

A direct user command sets the device and puts it on manual hold. Automation actions on a held device are skipped until the next "mode" event, which releases all holds before its rules fire. Commands do not trigger rules by themselves.
A lock cannot be set to locked while its door sensor reads open: the action is ignored (the lock keeps its value, and no change happens). Unlocking is always possible.
Thermostat setpoints (heat devices) are limited to the range 16-24: a larger or smaller value is stored as the nearest limit.

When a device actually changes value (caused by a user command or by a rule; no change if it already had that value), rules with trigger "device becomes value" are queued and fire after the current event's own rules, in the order the changes happened.
Value codes: on@N = light on at N % brightness, off, on/off for plugs, locked/unlocked, open/closed for blinds, a number = thermostat setpoint in °C.
